what: protocol v5 design panel (workflow v5-class-closing-design, run wf_a011ff7d-e47, 2026-09-24): three designers from different angles, two judges scoring every design against every red-team finding of rounds 1-3 (one soundness-first, one adoption/testability), one synthesizer. The synthesized spec is DESIGN_protocol_v5e_mint_anchor_2026_09_24.md. Scratch prototypes are not committed; the designs' experiments_run fields describe what each checked.

designs.name: v5e "mint-and-anchor": the narrowest sound coverage instrument
designs.one_paragraph: Replace the identity heuristics and the attribution heuristics with two constructions, each provable in one sentence. IDENTITY BY MINTING: at trace entry, each declared function object T gets a brand-new code object M_T = T.__code__.replace(), assigned as T.__code__ and restored at exit. A frame counts for T iff frame.f_code IS M_T and frame.f_globals IS T.__globals__. Factory products, decorator products, wraps siblings, pre-trace clones and vendored or exec'd copies all run a different code object, because CPython builds functions only from compiled constants (MAKE_FUNCTION) or by explicit construction, and M_T is never a compiled constant. So nested code and wrapped targets need not be refused at all: the object at the declared path, wrapper included, is what gets observed, and nothing is ever unwrapped. ATTRIBUTION BY STACK ANCHOR: sections are calls, cov.run(name, fn, *a) and await cov.run_async(name, afn, *a). The frame of that run call is the anchor. A hit is credited to an opening iff that opening's anchor is registered (open) and is on the hit frame's f_back chain, and no other open opening of the same tracer is on that chain. Threads, pool workers, library daemon threads, grandchildren, asyncio tasks, loop callbacks and after-close calls cannot reach a section's anchor. Parallel harnesses open their own sections, and the same section name may be open many times at once. HOOK: one module-level sys.setprofile function. It is installed only on a thread that opens a section, and refuses any foreign profiler rather than chaining it. It contains no try/except, takes no lock, and removes itself from any thread with nothing open. Its loss is detected at close by identity plus an install epoch. Every close-time finding is written into the trace, and score() reads it. Removed machinery: gc holder scans, unwrap, closure and f_locals identity, ContextVars, Thread.start interception, threading.setprofile, profiler chaining, and the impostor, ambiguous and after-close buckets. The P1 retro, run with the unmodified run_p1.degenerate, records exactly {styxx.power:reachable: 12} and refuses [V5:NOT_EXERCISED] naming exactly the other four functions, on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13. The price is disclosed over-blocking: off-stack work never counts, sections must be calls, foreign setprofile profilers refuse, and only plain functions can be declared. One residual in the identity class remains: a function explicitly built from T's own code object with T's own globals during the trace, called and then dropped before exit.
designs.target_identity_rule:
ONE SENTENCE: a frame counts for target T iff frame.f_code IS M_T — a fresh code object the tracer created at entry with T.__code__.replace() and published only by assigning it to T.__code__ — and frame.f_globals IS T.__globals__.

RESOLUTION (at tracer __enter__, all targets resolved before anything is touched): 'module:Q.u.a.l' -> importlib.import_module(module), then vars()[part] steps through that module and then classes only. There is no getattr, no descriptor or __getattr__ execution, no __wrapped__ following and no unwrap. The final object is accepted iff type(obj) is types.FunctionType, or it is a staticmethod/classmethod whose __func__ is one.
ACCEPTED: module-level functions; methods defined on the named class; closures and factory products bound to a module/class name (e.g. double = make_mul(2)); functools.wraps wrappers (the WRAPPER is the target); singledispatch dispatchers; dataclass-generated methods; functions with __class__ cells; generator, coroutine and async functions; functions whose original code object is shared with other functions.
REFUSED: [V5:UNRESOLVED] — the import raised (any Exception, including SyntaxError), or the name is absent from the namespace; PEP 562 lazy attributes and unimported submodules are named in the message. [V5:INHERITED] — a class step whose name is only in a base's __dict__. [V5:INSTANCE_PATH] — a mid-path step through a non-class (instance, SimpleNamespace, registry) or a module after the colon. [V5:NOT_A_FUNCTION] — builtins, C/Cython, lru_cache/cache, class-based update_wrapper wrappers, partial, property, bound method, singledispatchmethod. [V5:ALIAS] — two declared targets are one function object. [V5:CODE_SWAPPED] — an enclosing trace already minted T and T.__code__ is no longer its M_T. [V5:REENTRY] — a tracer entered twice.
TRIPWIRES FOR THE ONE REMAINING DOOR: [V5:CLONE_CALLED] — M_T ran with f_globals that are not T.__globals__, i.e. a function was built from T's code object, or exec(T.__code__, other_ns). This credits nothing and refuses every declaring gate. [V5:CLONE_ALIVE] — at exit, the refcount of M_T exceeds what T and the registry account for, and a gc.get_referrers scan (only then) finds another FunctionType holding M_T. [V5:CODE_SWAPPED] — at exit, T.__code__ is not M_T.

WHY THE CLASS CANNOT REOPEN: Python exposes no link from a frame to the function object being run except its code object (and globals). Minting makes the code-to-function map one-to-one for the life of the trace. CPython creates frames running code C only by calling a function whose __code__ is C, or by exec/eval of C. Functions acquire C only through MAKE_FUNCTION on a compiled constant, through FunctionType(C, ...), or through __code__ assignment. M_T is in no co_consts. So every non-T frame running M_T requires someone to take M_T out of T.__code__, or out of a live T frame, generator or traceback, during the trace and construct a function or exec from it.
- Factories, decorators with or without wraps, update_wrapper classes, per-call siblings, plugin registries built at import, vendored or exec'd copies, dataclass siblings, copy.copy/deepcopy (functions are atomic) and pickle (by reference) cannot do this.
- Because nothing is unwrapped, no two distinct callables are ever mapped to one observed code object. That many-to-one mapping was the root of R2-D2 and R3-D1.
- Everything previously refused as SHARED_CODE because the ORIGINAL code was shared now works, since sharing of the original is irrelevant.
- The residual is a clone with T's own globals, built during the trace from T's own code object, called and then dropped before exit. It is stated as a limit and never claimed closed.
designs.attribution_rule:
ONE SENTENCE: a counted frame is credited to opening O iff O's anchor — the frame of the cov.run()/cov.run_async() call that opened O — is registered (O is open) and is on the frame's f_back chain, and no other open opening of O's tracer is on that chain.

DETAILS:
- Sections are calls, not with-blocks: run(section, fn, /, *a, **k) opens, calls fn from its own frame, and closes on BOTH the except and the return path of that same frame. run_async does the same as a coroutine frame awaited directly by the caller's task. Opening and closing therefore always happen in one frame: per-stack LIFO by construction, no foreign-context exit, no ContextVar.
- At open: [V5:TRACE_INACTIVE] if the tracer is not active, [V5:UNDECLARED_SECTION], and [V5:NESTED_SECTION] if an open opening of the SAME tracer is on the opener's stack. Other tracers may nest; each credits its own openings, so nesting blinds neither.
- At a hit: the hook walks f_back to the root and collects registered anchors. For each tracer with exactly one anchor on the chain, it increments that opening's count for the tracer's name of T. With two or more, the hit goes to that opening's 'ambiguous' counter and credits nothing. This is only reachable by resuming a suspended coroutine of one opening inside another opening's flow; tested.
- At close: the anchor is deregistered before anything else, so nothing can credit O afterwards. At tracer exit, _by_code is emptied, so no credit is possible after exit, and every still-open opening gets [V5:OPEN_AT_EXIT].
- Close findings ([V5:PROFILER_LOST], [V5:THREAD_HOP]) and tracer findings ([V5:CODE_SWAPPED], [V5:CLONE_ALIVE], [V5:CLONE_CALLED], [V5:OPEN_AT_EXIT]) are appended to the trace. run() raises them only when no exception is in flight, so the original exception is never masked.
- score() refuses a declaring gate if the trace carries any tracer finding, if any opening of its section carries a finding, or if any opening's end is not 'returned' ([V5:SECTION_UNFINISHED]). It otherwise checks the union of calls over all openings of the section ([V5:NOT_EXERCISED]).

WHY THE CLASS CANNOT REOPEN: a frame's f_back chain consists of frames on the same thread that called it, directly or through C. Suspended coroutine chains rejoin a stack only when resumed by that stack. The chain of a thread, pool worker, library daemon thread, grandchild, asyncio Task, loop callback, Future callback or executor job begins at its own bootstrap or loop step, so it contains another flow's anchor only if that flow is literally running the loop. In that case the loop's tasks are inside that section by definition, and any section they try to open refuses NESTED_SECTION.
- Nothing is inherited, so no context copy, thread-start record, pool lifetime or shard name can carry credit anywhere.
- Calls after close cannot credit, because the anchor is gone.
- Concurrent sections cannot cross-credit: a frame is on one chain at a time, and the only-one-per-tracer clause handles resumed coroutines.
- Exception exits run the same close code.
- Refusals swallowed by the harness do not help it, because they are data in the trace, not only exceptions.
designs.mechanism:
sys.setprofile only, the same on 3.9–3.13, per thread and never threading.setprofile, plus code minting through __code__ assignment and frame anchors from sys._getframe(). No sys.monitoring, no patching of names, no ContextVars, and no gc at resolution or close.

HOOK RULES (one sentence): one module-level profile function, containing no try/except and taking no lock, installed with sys.setprofile only by an opening on its own thread, removed at that thread's last close, and removing itself on the first event on any thread with no open opening or once no trace is active.

LIFECYCLE:
(1) __enter__: resolve every target, check ALIAS, then under an RLock mint M_T for each T. Minting is refcounted in a global registry keyed by id(M_T) and id(T), whose entries hold the objects so ids cannot be reused. Nested or concurrent tracers declaring the same T share one M_T and one list of tracers.
(2) _open (in run/run_async): read sys.getprofile(). A non-None profiler that is not our hook refuses [V5:FOREIGN_PROFILER] before anything is installed; a foreign profiler is never called, chained, restored or replaced. If it is None, bump the thread's install epoch and install the hook. Increment the thread's open count, and register the anchor frame -> opening.
(3) Hook: if no trace is active, or this thread has no open opening, it calls sys.setprofile(None) and returns. Otherwise, on 'call' events only, it looks up id(frame.f_code) in the mint registry and checks identity (m.code is frame.f_code). On a globals mismatch it sets CLONE_CALLED and returns. On a hit it walks f_back to attribute the call. The per-opening counters are single-writer, because an anchor is on one stack at a time, so no lock is needed.
(4) _close: deregister the anchor. If closed on another thread, record [V5:THREAD_HOP]. Otherwise, if sys.getprofile() is not our hook or the thread's epoch changed since open, record [V5:PROFILER_LOST]: the hook was dropped by an exception raised in or while entering it (signal handler, KeyboardInterrupt, RecursionError) or replaced by the harness. Decrement the count, and at 0 remove the hook iff it is still ours.
(5) __exit__: empty _by_code, mark open openings OPEN_AT_EXIT, and convert clone flags to CLONE_CALLED. For each mint, drop this tracer; if T.__code__ is not M_T record CODE_SWAPPED, else restore the original when the last tracer leaves. The CLONE_ALIVE check does one sys.getrefcount per target and a gc.get_referrers scan only if unexplained references exist.
(6) record() is refused before exit ([V5:TRACE_ACTIVE]) and takes no lock; it copies dicts. Sections are recorded as lists of openings: {calls, ambiguous, end: returned|raised|open, problems}.
(7) score(): validate the trace (dict types, string keys, positive int counts, known [V5:...] problem codes, the end enum), then apply the attribution rule's scoring clause.

finding_closure.how: Frames are matched against M_T, minted per function object. Siblings sharing the ORIGINAL code (check_low/check_high from one _make; entry_a/entry_b behind one no-wraps decorator) run the original, never M_T, and MAKE_FUNCTION cannot produce M_T because it is in no co_consts. Tested: both refuse NOT_EXERCISED; the declared object itself passes. The one remaining door in the class — a function built during the trace from T's own code object with T's own globals, called and then dropped before exit — requires reading T.__code__ (or a T frame/generator/traceback) and constructing from it. It is a stated limit, with CLONE_ALIVE (live clone) and CLONE_CALLED (other globals) tripwires.

Identity only: registry lookup by id(M_T), whose entry holds M_T so the id cannot be reused, then `m.code is frame.f_code`. Vendored equal copies, an exec'd copy of the module and a sibling dataclass __init__ each have their own code object, which is never M_T. Tested: all three refuse NOT_EXERCISED.

There is no section slot. Credit requires the opener's own run() frame on the call's f_back chain. A thread started in A, or a task, has a chain rooted at its own bootstrap or loop step. Tested: thread from A calling while B is open, and a task created in A, credit neither section.

The hook never calls, chains, restores or replaces another profiler. A foreign sys.getprofile() at open refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER before anything is installed. Tested on 3.10/3.11: cProfile present gives FOREIGN_PROFILER and the user's Profile is still installed afterwards. On 3.12/3.13 cProfile runs on sys.monitoring, is invisible to getprofile, and coexists (scores PASS).

Sections are calls, so open and close are in one frame and LIFO per stack by construction. Tracers share one hook and a refcounted mint registry, so exit order is irrelevant. Tested: tracer A exited before B (both PASS, code restored, registry empty); two tracers in two threads interleaved on the same target (exact counts 3 and 5). Re-entering a tracer refuses REENTRY.

Resolution is import + vars() lookups + type checks. Only import can raise, and any Exception there is UNRESOLVED (tested RuntimeError at import). No unwrap is done, so a __wrapped__ loop cannot be reached, and no getattr/__getattr__ runs user code.

score() validates type(...) is dict/list/str/int at every level: targets keys, sections keys, opening dicts, calls keys, counts (bool refused), problems strings, known codes. check_metrics reports and never raises. Tested: non-string keys in targets, sections and calls; list/dict section formats; unknown problem code; bool count; undeclared key — all refuse with BAD_TRACE or BAD_COUNT.

Every refused honest shape is listed in over_blocking_costs, including threads/tasks/pools, pre-existing threads, _thread threads, and profilers inside sections. Parallel sections are now supported: each worker opens its own; tested 8 concurrent openings of one name, exact counts.

A class step reads only vars(cls); an inherited name refuses INHERITED (tested Sub.fit). Declaring the definer (Base.fit) credits any call of that one function object, which is literally what ran (tested). The fullmatch regex is kept from the existing DECL parse.

A decorator applied at runtime creates its product through MAKE_FUNCTION from the original inner code constant, so the product never runs M_T. Tested: timed(cheap_path)() inside the section with score_all declared refuses NOT_EXERCISED. No close-time gc re-check is needed.
Pool worker stacks never contain a section's anchor, so pooled work credits only a section the work item itself opens. Tested: B's job on a pool shared with concurrently open A credits A nothing.

threading.setprofile is never used. The hook exists on a thread only while that thread has an open opening, and removes itself on the first event otherwise, or when no trace is active. Tested: a harness reinstalling a saved hook after close sees it vanish after one event; pool threads end unhooked; threading.getprofile() is never touched.
The path grammar is one module, then classes only. Tested: instance path default_model.fit and SimpleNamespace NS.fit refuse INSTANCE_PATH with the offending type named.

No unwrapping: run_fast and run_safe are distinct wrapper objects with distinct observed code, and the declared wrapper is what is traced. Tested: declaring run_fast and calling run_safe refuses NOT_EXERCISED; calling run_fast passes.

The shape changed. A pool created anywhere, reused across sections, ThreadPool, executors and to_thread all work when the submitted function opens its own section (tested: to_thread(cov.run, 'G', target) passes; pool.map of cov.run passes). Work submitted from inside a section without its own section never counts (tested: to_thread(target) inside run_async gives NOT_EXERCISED). Listed in over_blocking_costs.

The hook has no handler, so a RecursionError raised in or while entering it propagates as CPython defines, and the drop is detected at close by hook identity plus install epoch, giving PROFILER_LOST with a message naming this route. There is no thread hook to leak. Tested on 3.10–3.13: recursion to the limit inside a section refuses PROFILER_LOST. The resulting over-block (harnesses that exercise the recursion limit) is disclosed.

No thread-level hook exists. The per-thread sys hook is removed by the last close on both the except and return paths of run(), with self-removal as a backstop. Tested: exception exits, KeyboardInterrupt and SIGALRM exits leave sys.getprofile() None and the bookkeeping empty.

The foreign-context exit half is structural: sections are calls, so there is no __exit__ callable from another Context and no ContextVar.reset. The check_metrics(non-dict) half is the existing report path, kept. Tested: None, [], 's' and 5 are reported unusable, never raised.

A factory product is built from the original lambda/closure constant and never runs M_T, so defaults and cells are irrelevant. Tested: double=make_mul(2) declared with make_mul(3)(5) called refuses NOT_EXERCISED; score_lenient declared with make_scorer(abs, True) called (same cells, other default) refuses NOT_EXERCISED; calling double passes. The only way to get a same-defaults-invisible impostor is the explicit in-trace clone from M_T (the stated R1-B1 residual).

Attribution never reads contextvars. A consumer task's stack begins at the loop step and does not contain A's run_async anchor. Tested: A lazily starts consumer tasks and B's job runs on them while both are open; A is credited 0 and B 0 (both refuse). Tasks opening their own run_async sections are attributed exactly (stress: 40 tasks plus unsectioned noise tasks, exact counts, 0 cross-credit, 3 runs × 4 versions).

The hook contains no try/except, so it cannot swallow anything. Tested: a SIGALRM Timeout(Exception) in a tight traced loop propagated in 20/20 trials on each of 3.10–3.13, with PROFILER_LOST recorded whenever it landed inside the hook (16–19/20); a KeyboardInterrupt from a signal propagated 5/5.

(a) A plain direct caller of the inner no longer satisfies a wraps wrapper (no unwrap): tested NOT_EXERCISED. (b) A class-based update_wrapper instance is refused NOT_A_FUNCTION: tested. (c) Per-call wraps siblings are separate products with original code: tested NOT_EXERCISED. (d) Reverse over-block removed: an undecorated score with two wraps aliases, called only via score_v1, passes.

Close runs in both branches of the one run() frame. Every finding is written into the trace, and score() refuses on any recorded finding and on any opening whose end is not 'returned'. Tested: a section raising, with the exception swallowed by the harness, refuses SECTION_UNFINISHED; a swallowed PROFILER_LOST or OPEN_AT_EXIT still refuses at score.

Neither the hook nor record() takes any lock; enter/exit/open/close share one RLock. Tested: cyclic garbage whose __del__ calls a target, collected at 39 swept gen-0 thresholds around open/close/record on 3.10–3.13, never deadlocked.

No gc at resolution or close. Measured on a 1M-object heap with 3 targets: per-section close 0.02–0.05 ms (current: 100–122 ms), tracer exit 0.01 ms. The refcount-gated gc scan runs only when something besides T holds M_T (17–19 ms, measured with a live generator of the target).
Other threads are never credited, so no THREAD_OUTLIVES check exists. Tested: a daemon thread started in the section and outliving it scores PASS on the section's own call.

A section name maps to a list of openings merged at score, so many concurrent shards of one name are fine (tested 8 in a pool; stress with up to 32 openings per name). The singledispatch dispatcher is a plain function, credited when called (tested PASS).
INSTANCE_PATH now names the type ('NS' is a SimpleNamespace, not a class) and says what to declare instead; the grammar refuses any non-class mid-path.
Still refused, deliberately: resolution never runs module __getattr__. The UNRESOLVED message names PEP 562 and unimported submodules; the fix is to declare the defining module.
No tracer-wide flag exists. Findings are per opening; PROFILER_LOST is judged per opening from hook identity and the thread's install epoch at its own open and close.
There is no chaining. A foreign profiler refuses at open and is left untouched, so an exception in our hook can drop only our hook.
f_locals is never read; closure identity is implied by minting. The remaining per-hit cost is the f_back walk: about 3.3–4.6 us per hit at depth 30 (disclosed).

Clones made at import or through a factory are not credited (tested REGISTRY[0]). A clone built during the trace from T.__code__ with T.__globals__ (and T.__closure__) and dropped before exit is credited — the stated residual. A live clone gives CLONE_ALIVE; other globals give CLONE_CALLED (both tested).

designs.p1_retro:
Run with papers/first-afference/run_p1.py UNMODIFIED, loaded as run_p1 against styxx/power_QUARANTINED.py.txt loaded as styxx.power, exactly as run_protocol_v5d.py does. The only change is in the exam runner: `cov.run("G4_refuses_degenerate", run_p1.degenerate, np.random.default_rng(run_p1.SEED))` replaces `with cov.section(...)`. P1's G4 carries exercises = [effective_n, order_stat_bar, false_positive_rate, min_detectable_bar, reachable].

On 3.10.20, 3.11.15, 3.12.3 and 3.13.12 alike:
- The section records exactly [{'calls': {'styxx.power:reachable': 12}, 'ambiguous': {}, 'end': 'returned', 'problems': []}], and degenerate_refusal_rate is 1.0.
- score() refuses with "[V5:NOT_EXERCISED] gate 'G4_refuses_degenerate': COVERAGE VIOLATION -- never executed ['styxx.power:effective_n', 'styxx.power:order_stat_bar', 'styxx.power:false_positive_rate', 'styxx.power:min_detectable_bar'] ... (did execute ['styxx.power:reachable'])". That is exactly the four unexercised functions.
- reachable.__code__ is restored and sys.getprofile() is None afterwards.

Minting is what makes this work unmodified: run_p1 imported `reachable` by name before the trace, and name patching would have missed every call; minting the function object's code catches calls through any captured reference.

Reported, not gated: P1's G1 re-run with exercises=[order_stat_bar] records order_stat_bar x1, reached transitively through reachable(n_draws>1), so it passes — the outcome the v5 prereg anticipated.
over_blocking_costs: Off-stack work never counts. Anything not called from inside fn on the section's own stack credits nothing (NOT_EXERCISED): threads and grandchildren started in the section; thread pools, executors, loop.run_in_executor, asyncio.to_thread, multiprocessing.pool.ThreadPool; library worker threads; asyncio tasks spawned inside run_async (create_task, gather, TaskGroup, ensure_future, shield, as_completed, wait_for on <=3.11); loop callbacks (call_soon, call_later, add_done_callback). Each worker, job or task must open its own section: cov.run inside the submitted function, or run_async inside the task. Exception: an event loop run inside cov.run (asyncio.run inside) puts all its tasks on the section's stack, and they count.

v5c/v5d valid cases this design refuses: thread_started_in_section, thread_pool_inside_section, x2_grandchild_thread_in_section, asyncio_task_in_one_section (when the loop runs outside the section), and preexisting_python_profiler_chained. The frozen v5d exam therefore cannot be reused; a v5e exam must be frozen before implementation.

`with cov.section(name):` no longer exists; sections are calls, cov.run(name, fn, ...) or await cov.run_async(...). A section cannot be opened from a helper context manager, a yield fixture or ExitStack. Passing a generator or coroutine function to run() does its work after the section closes, so it counts nothing.
Nested sections of one tracer on one stack refuse NESTED_SECTION. This includes tasks that try to open sections inside a loop that itself runs inside a section.

Any pre-existing sys.setprofile profiler on the thread refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER; a profiler started inside a section refuses PROFILER_LOST. Refused: cProfile/profile on <=3.11, profile.runcall, yappi, pyinstrument, pure-Python profilers. On 3.12+ cProfile uses sys.monitoring and coexists. settrace tools (coverage.py, pdb) are unaffected.

Any exception raised in or while entering the hook drops it, and the section refuses PROFILER_LOST even if the harness catches the exception and carries on. Causes: hitting the recursion limit, signal-handler exceptions (pytest-timeout's signal method), KeyboardInterrupt. A battery that deliberately exercises the recursion limit inside a section cannot be traced.
An exception escaping cov.run makes that opening 'raised', and the gate refuses SECTION_UNFINISHED. Expected exceptions (pytest.raises style) must be caught inside fn.

Only plain Python functions can be declared: module functions, methods on the defining class, staticmethod/classmethod, closures bound to a name, wraps wrappers. Refused: lru_cache/cache, class-based wrappers, functools.partial, properties, bound methods, singledispatchmethod, builtins/C/Cython, PEP 562 lazy attributes, paths through instances, namespaces or sub-modules, and inherited methods (declare the definer).
A wrapped target is the wrapper. A harness that calls the inner function directly (f.__wrapped__, or another reference to the inner) does not exercise the declared name.

During the trace, T.__code__ is a different (equal) object. Code that keys caches on code identity or compares f.__code__ by identity sees the change. Hot-reload tools that rewrite __code__ in place (IPython autoreload, jurigged) refuse CODE_SWAPPED. Test utilities that clone or rebind functions from their code refuse CLONE_ALIVE or CLONE_CALLED.
Two declared names for one function object refuse ALIAS; declare it once.
A section still running on another thread when the trace exits refuses OPEN_AT_EXIT. A manually driven coroutine section finished on another thread refuses THREAD_HOP.

Cost: every Python call on a thread with an open section pays the profile hook (about 0.4 us per event, similar to the current implementation). Every target hit also pays a full f_back walk: 100k hits at depth 30 took 0.33–0.46 s, against 0.11–0.14 s for the current implementation.
Child processes remain invisible (unchanged); their calls read as unexercised.
stated_limits: Exercised is not tested: one call with its result discarded satisfies a declaration (unchanged).
Transitive calls count: a target reached through another declared target is exercised (unchanged).
Declared only: a gate without 'exercises' is unchecked (unchanged).
The trace is runner-written: forgery of the result dict is out of scope (unchanged threat model).
Hardcoded values (P1's G3 defect) are out of scope (unchanged).

Class A residual, never claimed closed: a function constructed DURING the trace from T's own code object — read from T.__code__, or from a live T frame's f_code, a T generator's gi_code or a traceback — with T's own globals, called and then dropped before the trace exits, is credited as T. It requires explicit code-object construction (FunctionType/exec/__code__ assignment). No factory, decorator, MAKE_FUNCTION, copy or pickle path reaches M_T. It is caught if the clone is alive at exit (CLONE_ALIVE) or runs under other globals (CLONE_CALLED).

Code that CPython runs on the section's own stack without the harness calling it counts for that section: signal handlers, __del__/weakref finalizers and gc callbacks triggered there, import-time module code. Calls made by settrace/setprofile callbacks are not observed.
A harness that saves sys.getprofile() and later reinstalls our hook blinds that window without a PROFILER_LOST record. This can only under-count, so it can only cause a refusal.

An asynchronous exception landing in the few bytecodes between run()'s registration and its try leaves the opening 'open' (refused as SECTION_UNFINISHED or OPEN_AT_EXIT). It may leave that thread's hook installed until no trace is active.
Counts are frame entries: generator and coroutine resumptions count again (tested: a two-yield generator records 3). Coverage needs only >= 1.
A generator or coroutine created in one section and resumed in another is credited where it runs, the resumer's section: the code executed in that flow.

Re-entry of open/close from a finalizer or signal handler on the same thread is serialized by an RLock rather than deadlocking. Credit cannot result from partially updated bookkeeping, because it requires a registered anchor of an open opening on the stack; the worst case is a spurious PROFILER_LOST.
CPython only. Greenlet/gevent stack switching and free-threaded 3.13t are untested. 3.9 is not executed (no interpreter available).
Tracer ID bumped to coverage_trace/2: committed v5/v5c/v5d results carrying /1 traces must be re-scored with their pinned implementation, not this one.

designs.name: v5e "lower-bound trace": one-owner carriers for identity, opener-stack ownership for attribution
designs.one_paragraph:
Three rounds of patches kept failing because v5 rests on two wrong primitives. For identity (class A), it treats a code object plus frame state (globals, closure cells) as "the declared function ran". For attribution (class B), it credits whichever section name a unit inherited. Each patch closed the instance it was shown, and the adversary came back through another door into the same class. v5e replaces both primitives, and every count becomes a lower bound.

IDENTITY. A target is traced through one "carrier" function. The compiler must not have marked the carrier's code CO_NESTED, so the only thing that ever instantiates it is a module or class body, and that body finished running before resolution. The carrier must be the only live function holding that code when tracing starts. If the declared object is a wrapper, the carrier must be held only by that wrapper. The first credited call per (target, section) re-checks that the carrier is still the only live holder. That check is exact, because a calling function is alive and visible to the garbage collector during its own call.

ATTRIBUTION. Each time a section is entered, a fresh instance is created that remembers the frame of its with-statement (the opener). A call is DIRECT when the opener frame is on the calling stack inside the same coroutine unit and the context variable holds that instance. Everything else is INHERITED: threads, tasks, callbacks, context copies, and concurrent.futures work items (which carry their submitter's section). An INHERITED call counts only while its instance is open and is the only open instance.

MECHANICS. Nothing detected at close can change a verdict, so there is no close-time check to skip or swallow. Hook mishaps only lose calls and are recorded as notes. The hook re-raises every exception except RecursionError and MemoryError. Any thread holding the lock is marked busy, and the hook ignores busy threads, so re-entry cannot deadlock. score() refuses only on a bad declaration, zero credited calls, or a malformed or stale trace.

BREADTH KEPT. Decorated entry points (functools.wraps stacks, lru_cache, contextmanager), thread pools and asyncio inside a section, one executor reused across sequential sections (even when warmed outside them), to_thread, ThreadPool, library daemon threads, two threads each opening a section with the same name, and per-item sections that exit by exception all score. Tested.

WHERE BREADTH COSTS SOUNDNESS, exactly three places:
- A decorated target is defined as its undecorated body, so a call through `__wrapped__` counts.
- Inherited credit while only one section is open admits work handed to that section's workers through user queues by code outside every section.
- Code the runtime injects onto a section's own stack (signal handlers, finalizers) counts for that section.

WHERE SOUNDNESS COSTS BREADTH. While two sections overlap, only each section's own with-block stack counts. Nested-code and multi-route targets cannot be declared.

The prototype passes 108/108 checks on each of 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, and the P1 retro-case is exact on all four. Eight cases in the frozen v5d exam change their expected outcome under this design, so v5e needs its own frozen prereg and a round-4 red team before any shipping claim.
designs.target_identity_rule:
RESOLUTION. `module:qualname` is resolved by walking own dicts only:
- a module's `__dict__`, falling back to the module's PEP 562 `__getattr__` only when the module defines one;
- a class's own `__dict__`; if an ancestor defines the name instead, refuse INHERITED;
- an instance's own `__dict__` (e.g. SimpleNamespace, registry objects); a class-provided attribute reached through an instance refuses INSTANCE_PATH.
staticmethod and classmethod unwrap to `__func__`. Any exception raised during import, the attribute steps, or the `__wrapped__` walk (loop-detected, at most 64 steps) refuses UNRESOLVED.

CARRIER. Starting from the declared object D, the carrier is the first object on D's `__wrapped__` chain that is a FunctionType whose code lacks CO_NESTED. When D is itself a plain module-level or class-level def, D is its own carrier and nothing is unwrapped. So a `@functools.wraps(_run) def run_fast` is traced as run_fast.

REFUSED AT ENTRY:
- NESTED_CODE: the chain ends at a nested function, i.e. factory products, closures, decorator wrappers without functools.wraps, dataclass/attrs-generated methods, methods of classes built inside functions.
- NO_CODE: a non-function with no `__wrapped__` (builtins, partial, property, bound-method aliases, JIT dispatchers).
- SHARED_CODE: after one gc.collect() and ONE gc.get_referrers(*all_codes) pass, a carrier's code has another live FunctionType holder, or two targets share a carrier (alias).
- SHARED_ROUTE: D is not the carrier, and some link of the chain has a GC referrer the link above does not hold directly. "Held directly" means the wrapper object itself (a C-level wrapper's slots), its own referents (`__dict__`, defaults, closure tuple), or its closure cells. Only frames on the resolving stack are ignored. So module globals, sibling wrappers, registries (even one captured in the closure), suspended generators, and live objects holding the inner function all refuse.

AT CALL TIME. A call matches only by id(frame.f_code) plus an `is` check; equality is never used. The first credited call per (target, section name) runs one gc.get_referrers(code) and is credited only if the carrier is the sole live FunctionType holder. A failed check sends the call to `uncredited.shared_code` and is retried at most once per new section instance.

ACCEPTED: plain module functions, module-level lambdas, methods/staticmethods/classmethods of module-level classes (credited when called through subclasses too, because the object is the defining class's), functools.wraps stacks, lru_cache, contextmanager, a class-based update_wrapper decorator that is the sole wrapper, own-dict namespace paths.

WHY THE CLASS CANNOT REOPEN:
1. The compiler sets CO_NESTED on exactly the code objects that are re-instantiated each time an enclosing function runs; the 20-row table matched on 3.10–3.13. An accepted carrier is therefore instantiated only by its module or class body, which has already finished.
2. Any other function running that code must come from explicit metaprogramming (FunctionType(...), `__code__` assignment). Such a function is alive and GC-visible during its own call, so the call-time holder check sees it. Defaults, closures, kwdefaults and globals are never consulted, so there is no per-function state for an impostor to match.
3. For wrappers, every route to the carrier either existed at entry (and was refused unless the wrapper owns it) or was taken from the declared wrapper itself (`__wrapped__`, its closure), which is calling its body.
The only remaining door is execution with no function object at all, which exists only on 3.9/3.10 (see stated limits).
designs.attribution_rule:
SECTION INSTANCES. Each section entry creates a fresh instance {name, serial, opener, open}. The opener is the frame whose with-statement entered the section, skipping contextlib frames and the generators contextlib drives (ExitStack, a user @contextmanager wrapper).

ATTRIBUTION, computed once per watched call:
1. Walk frame.f_back from the call.
   - If an open instance's opener frame is reached AND the tracer's ContextVar holds that same instance, the call is DIRECT.
   - If a `concurrent.futures._WorkItem.run` frame is reached first, the call takes the section that item recorded, as INHERITED.
   - The walk stops at a unit boundary: a coroutine frame whose f_back is not a coroutine frame, meaning a task base or a manual driver.
2. Otherwise, if the ContextVar holds an instance (tasks, callbacks, copied contexts), INHERITED.
3. Otherwise, the section recorded at Thread.start for the current thread, INHERITED.
4. Otherwise, unsectioned.
Thread.start and `_WorkItem.__init__` record the attribution of the stack that calls them, keeping the instance but always as INHERITED. Work items are INHERITED rather than DIRECT because a long-running item (a queue consumer) can execute another section's jobs. My first draft made items DIRECT; I built that exact attack and it passed, and making items INHERITED closed it.

CREDIT RULE. A call is credited iff, at call time, its instance is open AND (the call is DIRECT OR that instance is the only open instance in the tracer). Otherwise it goes to the after_close, ambiguous or unsectioned bucket, and those buckets count for nothing.

WHY THE CLASS CANNOT REOPEN. Every mechanism that moves work off the opener's own stack is non-DIRECT by construction, including mechanisms nobody has named yet. That covers threads, grandchildren, pools, asyncio tasks, call_soon/call_later handles, copy_context().run, run_coroutine_threadsafe onto a loop running inside the section, executor items, and library daemons. DIRECT requires two things: the opener frame on the current stack within the current coroutine unit, and the section's own context. A non-DIRECT call is credited only under exclusivity, evaluated at call time against the tracer's global set of open instances. An instance never reopens: a later section with the same name is a new instance. Closing an instance happens in `__exit__`, which runs on every exit path.

So three things cannot happen, whatever created the descendant:
- a descendant of A credits A (or B) while both A and B are open;
- a descendant of a closed A credits a later A or B;
- a unit descended from no section credits the open section.
Every class-B door from the three rounds is an instance of one of these.

WHAT DIRECT DOES ADMIT. Anything executing on the with-block's own stack in its own context. That is the definition of "inside the section", and it is why hand-offs through user queues and runtime-injected calls are stated limits rather than doors.

BREADTH PRICE. While two or more instances are open, work in a thread, task, item or callback counts for neither. Sequential sections keep every pool, task and executor shape.
designs.mechanism:
OBSERVATION. The tracer uses sys.setprofile in the entering thread and threading.setprofile for threads started afterwards. Each installed hook is a `_Hook` chained to any Python-level profiler already present. A non-Python profiler in either slot refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER before any slot is written, and a C profiler present at entry is left installed. On 3.12+ cProfile uses sys.monitoring and simply coexists with the tracer.

HOT PATH. Only 'call' events are processed. Each one costs a single dict lookup of id(frame.f_code) in a watch table holding the carriers, Thread.start and `_WorkItem.__init__`. One code object can carry several handlers, which is why declaring `threading:Thread.start` now works. Handlers run only on a hit, and only if the current thread is not in the tracer's busy set.
- The busy set covers the hook body, section bookkeeping and record(), so finalizers, signal handlers and the hook's own allocations never re-enter.
- The lock is taken only for small commits, and only by busy threads; heap scans run outside the lock.
- The hook catches only RecursionError and MemoryError, records a note, and stays installed. Every other BaseException is noted and re-raised; CPython then drops the chain, which loses calls but fails closed.
- The stack walk runs only on hits: about 2–3 µs per target call against 1.2–1.5 µs today. Non-target profiled calls cost the same as today (fib(22): 28 ms vs 31 ms).

TRACER LIFECYCLE.
- `__enter__` refuses REENTRY and FOREIGN_PROFILER.
- `__exit__` never raises. It restores a slot only if that slot holds its own hook or is empty, and when empty it restores the pre-entry profiler (so Ctrl-C no longer loses a chained user profiler). Every restore skips exited hooks. It marks the tracer exited; exited hooks become inert and remove themselves from whichever thread next calls them. Unclosed sections are recorded as notes.

SECTION LIFECYCLE. Sections are class-based context managers.
- `__enter__` refuses UNDECLARED_SECTION, TRACER_INACTIVE and NESTED_SECTION (an open instance in the ContextVar, or a DIRECT open instance on the stack), then creates the instance and sets the ContextVar.
- `__exit__` never raises. It sets the instance's `open` flag to False, resets the ContextVar (a ValueError becomes a note), and records a note if the hook is no longer installed.

COST. One gc.collect() and one gc.get_referrers(*codes) pass at entry, plus route checks for wrapped targets. After that, at most one heap pass per (target, section name), and none at close.

RECORD. Tracer id `styxx.protocol.coverage_trace/2`; gates sha256; targets; `sections` as {name: {target: credited count}}; `uncredited` as {after_close, ambiguous, shared_code, unsectioned}; notes; `complete` (informational only).

SCORE. score() validates the whole trace shape in one pass before reading any of it. It then checks, in order: WRONG_TRACER, BAD_TRACE, STALE_TRACE, TARGET_SET, SECTION_ABSENT, BAD_COUNT, NOT_EXERCISED. The NOT_EXERCISED message lists that section's uncredited calls and the notes.

finding_closure.how: A carrier must have non-CO_NESTED code: factory closures (check_low/check_high) and no-wraps wrappers (entry_a) refuse NESTED_CODE at entry (tested). It must be the sole live holder at entry (SHARED_CODE), and the first credited call re-verifies sole holdership. No other door: any function running the code is alive and visible to the garbage collector during its own call, so a second holder is seen at the verified moment. Execution with no function object at all exists only on 3.9/3.10 and is a stated limit; on 3.11+ both variants are refused (tested).

The watch table is keyed by id(code), with an `is` check against the carrier's own code; equality is never consulted. A vendored equal-code copy and an exec'd copy of the whole module both refuse NOT_EXERCISED. A dataclass-generated __init__ is nested code and refuses NESTED_CODE (all tested on 3.10–3.13).

Section values are fresh instances, credit requires the instance to be open, and non-DIRECT credit requires it to be the only open instance. All of these refuse NOT_EXERCISED (tested): a thread from A calling during B, a background thread started outside sections, a task created in A awaited in B, call_later from A firing in B, copy_context() from A run in B, and a grandchild thread started after A closed. Every hand-off path is non-DIRECT by construction; see attribution_rule.

A non-Python profiler in either slot refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER before anything is written, and the C profiler is still installed afterwards (tested). The tracer only chains Python-level profilers, and exit only restores slots holding its own hook or empty slots, restoring a pre-entry profiler that was checked at entry. On 3.12+ cProfile runs on sys.monitoring and coexists with the tracer (tested).

Exited hooks are inert and remove themselves; every restore skips exited hooks; entering an active or exited tracer refuses REENTRY. An out-of-order exit is only a note, and both traces still score correctly (tested); no leaked profiler appeared in any of the 432 checks.

Import, attribute steps and the bounded, cycle-detected __wrapped__ walk sit inside one refusal boundary, so anything raised becomes UNRESOLVED. Tested: RuntimeError at import, SyntaxError, and a __wrapped__ loop through non-functions. A self-wrapped module function (`f.__wrapped__ = f`) no longer loops, because the walk stops at the first non-nested function.

score() validates the whole trace shape in one pass before reading anything: keys at all levels, dict-valued sections, uncredited buckets and notes. 14 malformed traces refuse with their named code, and check_metrics on None, [], "s" and 5 reports instead of raising: 18/18 on every version.

Several of round 1's over-blocks are gone: two threads each in their own section now score direct calls, and cProfile coexists on 3.12+. What remains is listed in over_blocking_costs: threads that predate the trace, _thread-started threads, and a profiler replaced inside a section on 3.9–3.11 (which blinds that thread).

Carried over: a class step requires the class's own __dict__ (INHERITED), and targets are matched with a full-string regex (a trailing newline refuses DECL; tested). Instance steps now require the instance's own __dict__.

A target decorated without functools.wraps is nested code and cannot be declared at all (NESTED_CODE; tested with score_all). A function created at runtime from a carrier's code, whether a FunctionType clone or a `__code__` swap, is a second live holder at its own call and is never credited (both tested, NOT_EXERCISED with shared_code recorded). The argument is the same as for R1-B1; no per-function state is ever consulted.

Pool workers are INHERITED units, and executor work items carry their submitter's section, also as INHERITED. Any inherited call while two instances are open is ambiguous. Tested: A's executor running B's job, A's raw queue-worker thread, and A's long-running consumer work item (a door in my own first draft, closed by making items INHERITED). All refuse for A, with the call recorded as ambiguous or credited to B's own submission.
Keeps v5d's self-removing inert hook. A worker started during the trace reports sys.getprofile() as None after its first event following exit (tested on 3.10–3.13).

A step through an instance accepts only that instance's own __dict__, so default_model.fit, which comes from the class, refuses INSTANCE_PATH (tested). SimpleNamespace and registry namespaces are accepted (tested).

When the declared object has its own non-nested code it is its own carrier and nothing is unwrapped: run_fast is traced as itself, so calling run_safe_w refuses NOT_EXERCISED (tested). Real wrappers unwrap only when the inner function is held directly by the wrapper; otherwise SHARED_ROUTE.

Sequential shapes now score (tested): an executor warmed outside sections and reused by two sections, to_thread and run_in_executor(None) in sequence, multiprocessing ThreadPool with terminate-without-join, and library daemon threads. Still refused and disclosed (tested): concurrent sections sharing one executor, to_thread under concurrent async gates, executors whose workers predate the tracer, and workers of a multiprocessing ThreadPool created outside any section.

Counts are lower bounds and no refusal code depends on hook health. The hook swallows only RecursionError/MemoryError, its own synchronous failures, and records a note. A RecursionError CPython raises while entering the hook drops it, which only loses calls and is noted at close. A6a (RecursionError caught inside a section) scores with notes and leaves the profiler clean (tested).

The tracer's __exit__ runs on every with-exit, including exception exits, and resets the threading slot if it holds this tracer's hook; inert hooks remove themselves. After an exception exit, both the sys and threading slots are None (tested).

A ValueError from ContextVar.reset is caught and recorded as a note. The instance is closed regardless, because credit is keyed on instance.open, and a closed instance left in a context never blocks a later section (tested: G entered and exited in different tasks, then H opens fine). check_metrics on a non-dict reports (tested).

Factory products (`lambda x, k=k`, or one closure with different defaults) have CO_NESTED code and refuse NESTED_CODE at entry (P1 and P2 tested). No other door: the design never identifies a function through per-function state (defaults, cells, globals). It requires a code object instantiated by exactly one function, and verifies that at the credited call.

The stack walk stops at a task base (a coroutine driven by a non-coroutine), and DIRECT also requires the ContextVar to hold the instance. So tasks, handles and foreign coroutines, even on a loop running inside A's with-block, are INHERITED and ambiguous while B is open. Tested: t12's lazily started worker tasks, run_coroutine_threadsafe from B, and call_soon_threadsafe from B onto a loop inside A all refuse for A.

The hook re-raises every BaseException except RecursionError/MemoryError. CPython drops the chain (fail-closed, noted), and exit restores the pre-entry profiler when the slot is empty. A SIGALRM Timeout was delivered 20/20 on each of 3.10–3.13. Ctrl-C with a chained user profiler: the interrupt reached the harness and the profiler was restored 10/10 (8/10 in my first draft, fixed by restoring whenever the slot is empty).

T01a (a plain caller of the inner) refuses NOT_EXERCISED because run_fast is its own carrier. T01b (class-based update_wrapper siblings) refuses SHARED_ROUTE. T01c (a per-call wraps sibling) refuses NOT_EXERCISED. T01d (an undecorated target with two wraps aliases) now scores, and so does a call through an alias (transitive). The ownership test is direct, so a registry captured in the wrapper's closure and a suspended generator holding the inner function both refuse SHARED_ROUTE. The generator case appears as a frame referrer on 3.10, which was a second door in my own draft, closed by skipping only frames on the current stack.

There are no close-time checks. Closing an instance only flips instance.open, inside __exit__, which runs on every exit path. Every condition that could over-credit is decided per call at call time, and mishaps only lose calls, so no refusal exists that an exception exit could skip or a try/except could swallow. T02a–d refuse NOT_EXERCISED: clones are never verified, and a straggler thread's call lands in after_close for its own instance. Per-item sections that exit by exception still score (all tested).

Invariant: every thread holding the tracer lock is in the busy set, and the hook ignores busy threads; heap scans run outside the lock. A sweep of GC thresholds 1–25 at three sites (record, section, hook) found 0 hangs on each of 3.10–3.13. A mutant whose record() holds the lock without the busy mark hangs at k=10, 11 and 12, so the sweep does detect the defect.

There is no gc work at close. The whole cost is one gc.collect() plus one gc.get_referrers(*codes) pass at entry, and at most one pass per (target, section name) at the first credited call. Measured per section (open, 5 target calls, close), amortised over 200 sections: 0.10 / 0.17 / 0.30 ms at 0.1M / 1M / 3M heap objects, against 30 / 71 ms for the current implementation at 0.1M / 1M. Construction takes 26–106 ms.

THREAD_OUTLIVES is removed: a descendant that outlives its instance credits nobody (after_close). A never-joined daemon thread started in a section scores (tested). multiprocessing ThreadPool terminate-without-join also scores.

Same section name in two shards is closed structurally: they are two instances, and A6b scores {f: 2} (tested). singledispatch entry points still over-block, now disclosed and explained: they refuse SHARED_ROUTE at entry because the dispatch registry is a second route to the base function, and registered implementations would not count anyway. The author must declare the registered implementations under their own names (tested).

SimpleNamespace and registry own-dict steps are accepted (tested). PEP 562 module __getattr__ is used when the name is absent from the module dict (tested). Hook failures are notes, never sticky refusals. The profiler is restored when the slot is empty (Ctrl-C 10/10). f_locals is gone from the hot path because frame identity is removed; it is read only at Thread.start, at _WorkItem.__init__, and when the walk passes a work-item frame. A closure clone with identical cell contents is now a second live holder and is not credited.

over_blocking_costs: NESTED_CODE: targets whose code the compiler marks nested cannot be declared. This covers factory products and closures (double = make_mul(2)), entry points decorated without functools.wraps, methods of classes defined inside functions, generated methods (dataclass/attrs __init__, __eq__), and module functions returned by builder functions. The author must declare the module-level function those call.

SHARED_ROUTE: a decorated target whose inner function is reachable other than through its wrapper refuses. Examples: singledispatch entry points, entry = deco(raw) with raw still bound in the module, two wrappers of one function, a registry holding the inner function, or any live object holding it at entry (e.g. a pending contextmanager instance).
SHARED_CODE at entry: several live functions from one module-level def (lambdas made in a module-level loop), or two declared names for one function.

NO_CODE / INSTANCE_PATH / INHERITED: bound-method aliases (run = _default.run), functools.partial, property and cached_property, C and JIT callables (numba and similar never run their Python code), attributes a class provides through an instance, and inherited methods.

The overlap rule, which is the main breadth cost: while two or more section instances are open anywhere in the tracer, only calls on each section's own with-block stack count. Threads, asyncio child tasks (gather), executor items, to_thread/run_in_executor and callbacks in overlapping sections count for neither, which refuses NOT_EXERCISED (tested). This also affects sections opened in fixtures or wrapped in async context managers while running concurrently.

Workers reused across sections: raw threads, asyncio tasks and multiprocessing.pool.ThreadPool workers started in one section credit nobody in the next section. concurrent.futures executors are the exception, because their work items carry the submitter's section.

Invisible threads: threads that predate the tracer, including an executor warmed at import time (tested), threads started via _thread.start_new_thread, and workers of a multiprocessing ThreadPool created outside every section (unsectioned).

Profilers: on 3.9–3.11, a C profiler present at entry refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER, and one started inside a section blinds that thread; calls made under it are not counted (tested). 3.12+ coexists with cProfile.
Calls made only from inside profiler or trace callbacks (another tracer's hook, a user's profile function) are invisible. lru_cache hits do not execute the target and are not counted.
Child processes are invisible (carried from earlier rounds).
NESTED_SECTION: sections cannot nest on one stack, or in a task created inside an open section. A thread started inside a section may open its own section (sharding).

Committed v5-family results carry tracer/1 traces, which refuse WRONG_TRACER under v5e. This is intended, because those counts were attributed under rules now known to be unsound. Their committed verdicts stand as history, and the differential excludes them, as v5d already did.
stated_limits: Exercised is not tested: one credited call on one input satisfies a declaration (carried).

Transitive calls count. For a decorated target, the target IS its undecorated body, so a call obtained from the wrapper (entry.__wrapped__(x), inspect.unwrap, its closure) counts as the declared entry point, even though the decorator's own code did not run.

Attribution certifies WHERE a call executed (the with-block's own stack in its own context, or a descendant unit while its section was the only one open), not WHO asked for it. Work handed in through user data structures counts for the section that executes it. Two cases: the with-block drains a queue fed by others; or, while it is the only open section, code outside every section feeds that section's workers (tested: scores).

Code the runtime injects onto a section's own stack counts for that section: signal handlers, cyclic-GC finalizers, weakref callbacks and audit hooks. This holds even for an object belonging to a concurrently open section (tested: scores). A gc.callbacks start/stop flag could exclude cyclic-GC finalizers; I did not adopt it, to keep the invariant set small.

3.9/3.10 only: running a declared function's bare code object (exec(f.__code__)), or resuming a generator whose cloned function was freed before its first next(), is credited as the declared function (tested on 3.10). On 3.11+ the interpreter keeps a function object alive, and both are refused as shared (tested).

Schedulers that use neither coroutines nor contextvars (generator trampolines, greenlets) are treated as part of the section's own stack when run inside a with-block. greenlet, gevent and trio are untested.
The trace is written by the runner. Forgery is the accepted residual: hand-edited counts, rewritten co_flags or code objects, and C-level references hidden from the garbage collector.
Declared only: gates without 'exercises' get no check. G3's hardcoded-baseline defect is out of scope (carried).
Counts are lower bounds. Hook, profiler and context mishaps are recorded as notes and never refuse by themselves. A tracer blinded by the harness's own profiler reads as unexercised, not as an error.
Python 3.9 and free-threaded 3.13t were not executed.

Process: the frozen v5d exam cannot score v5e, because 8 of its violation cases change expected outcome. rt_factory_closure_sibling, rt_nowraps_decorator_sibling and rt2_runtime_nowraps_kept_alive become NESTED_CODE. rt2_wraps_siblings_share_inner becomes NOT_EXERCISED. rt_thread_outlives_section, rt_cprofile_inside_section, rt_out_of_order_exit and rt2_section_exited_in_other_context become notes with a count-determined outcome. v5e needs its own prereg with a frozen exam, and a round-4 red team, before any shipping claim.

INSTANCE_PATH: an instance step reaches an attribute outside that instance's own __dict__

designs.name: v5m: private replica + live stack
designs.one_paragraph: A profiler is a reasonable primitive; the mistake was what it was asked to identify. Python shares code objects by design, so "this code object ran" can never mean "this function ran". Under v5m, the code object being observed is made private. At trace entry each declared function object F gets F.__code__ = F.__code__.replace(): an equal but distinct code object that nothing else holds, restored at exit. A start of that replica is a call of F through any reference, including P1's from-import alias. Nothing that shares the original code ever runs it: factory products, closures, wraps and no-wraps siblings, class wrappers, vendored or exec'd copies, pre-trace clones. Attribution drops all inherited state (ContextVar, thread-start lineage, ambiguity rules). A start counts for section-opening O only if O's marker frame is on the executing thread's live f_back chain before any asyncio dispatch frame, and O is still open. The marker is either the frame running O's `with` statement or a frame the author explicitly bound to O with cov.carry(). Observation uses sys.monitoring local PY_START events on the replicas only (3.12+), or a per-thread setprofile hook that exists only while that thread holds a marker (3.9–3.11). The observer takes no lock and re-raises everything. It never refuses: every problem goes into the record, and score() reads it there. The result is that every round-1 to round-3 blocker is closed by construction, and a scratch prototype passes all of them on 3.10–3.13. The P1 retro is exact with run_p1.py unmodified. The price is stated plainly: work on other threads, pools or asyncio tasks counts only when carried, and non-function targets (lru_cache, partial, callable instances) cannot be declared. The one residual attribution door is another gate's work that the section's own with-block runs synchronously.
designs.target_identity_rule:
ACCEPTED: the object bound at "module:qualname" when the trace is entered, provided it is a types.FunctionType. Resolution rules:
- Module steps use inspect.getattr_static. They fall back to getattr only when the module defines a PEP 562 __getattr__.
- Class steps go only through that class's own __dict__.
- Non-module, non-class steps go only through that object's own instance __dict__. This allows SimpleNamespace and registry slots.
- staticmethod and classmethod resolve to __func__.
- NOTHING IS UNWRAPPED: no inspect.unwrap and no __wrapped__. A @functools.wraps wrapper is declared as itself, so only calls through that wrapper count.
- Aliases (two declared names bound to one function) are accepted. It is one object with one replica, so one call credits both names.
- A singledispatch function resolves to its dispatch wrapper function and counts when dispatched through.

REFUSED at trace entry, before any work runs:
- [V5:DECL]: malformed or non-ASCII strings, including a trailing newline.
- [V5:UNRESOLVED]: any exception while importing or getting attributes.
- [V5:INHERITED]: a class step naming an attribute that is only inherited.
- [V5:INSTANCE_PATH]: an attribute reached through an instance but found on its class, e.g. default_model.fit.
- [V5:NO_CODE]: anything that is not a FunctionType. That includes builtins, C wrappers such as lru_cache and cache, functools.partial, callable instances (including class-based update_wrapper wrappers), property, singledispatchmethod, bound methods, and Cython or numba functions.

WHY THE CLASS CANNOT REOPEN. The credit predicate is `frame.f_code is replica(F)`: an id-keyed lookup followed by `is`, so equality is never consulted. replica(F) is created by the tracer, and user code can reach it only as F.__code__. A frame can therefore run it only if:
- (i) F itself was called, through any reference: a module attribute, a from-import alias, a closure cell, a registry dict, a partial, a bound method or super(); or
- (ii) code read F.__code__ during the trace and built, assigned or exec'd another function with it.

Every sharing mechanism in rounds 1–3 shares the ORIGINAL code, which is never observed. That covers closures, factory products and defaults, no-wraps decorators (including runtime decoration), wraps siblings, per-call siblings, class wrappers, dataclass-generated __init__, vendored or exec'd module copies, and clones made before the trace. None of them can produce a credit. Case (ii) needs a deliberate code-level clone made inside the trace. It is detected as [V5:CODE_CLONED] if the clone is still alive at trace exit (one gc.get_referrers pass), and is a stated residual otherwise. No holder counting, wrapper scanning or frame globals/closure matching remains to be fooled.
designs.attribution_rule:
WHICH CALLS COUNT. At every start of a replica, walk frame.f_back from the target's frame, stopping at the first of two boundaries:
- a frame whose code is asyncio.events.Handle._run (an event-loop dispatch; the call is bucketed 'dispatched' and credited nowhere); or
- the bottom of the thread (bucketed 'unattributed').

For each tracer observing the target, the FIRST marker of that tracer met on the way decides. There are two kinds of marker:
- (a) The frame executing a `with cov.section(name):` statement. It is registered at __enter__ and removed at __exit__, so it exists for exactly the lifetime of that with-block. __enter__ verifies that the caller's f_lasti is at SETUP_WITH (3.9/3.10) or BEFORE_WITH (3.11–3.13). It hops through @contextlib.contextmanager helpers to the with-statement that uses the helper. ExitStack, pytest fixtures, a manual __enter__ and asynccontextmanager helpers refuse [V5:SECTION_FORM] at open, before the work runs.
- (b) The frame of one invocation of a cov.carry(fn) wrapper, sync or coroutine. It is bound to the opening in whose synchronous chain carry() was called; outside one, carry refuses [V5:CARRY_OUTSIDE].

The call is credited to that opening if it is still open, and otherwise bucketed 'after_close'. The same walk at section enter refuses [V5:NESTED_SECTION] within one tracer. Different tracers may nest, and each credits its own opening, so a self-tracing exam works.

Nothing else carries a section: no ContextVar, no thread-start lineage, no task or context lineage, no time window, no global slot, no ambiguity heuristic. Counts go into per-thread dicts with no lock. Section-time refusals are raised AND written to record()['problems']. score() refuses a gate whose section or targets appear in problems, and otherwise requires every declared target to appear in the section's counts.

WHY THE CLASS CANNOT REOPEN. A frame is on the chain only while it is executing and transitively waiting on this very call. That rules out each door found in rounds 1–3:
- Threads, pool workers, library daemon threads and grandchildren begin their chains at their own bootstrap.
- asyncio tasks reach their driver only through Handle._run, which cuts the walk.
- Context copies are never read.
- Concurrent sections, including two shards with the same name, each see only their own chain.
- A closed section has no marker, and a carry frame checks that its opening is still open.
- There are no close-time checks for an exception exit to skip.
- A swallowed raise remains in the record.

The only ways to be credited to O are to be synchronously awaited by O's with-block, or by a frame the author explicitly carried to O.

RESIDUAL DOOR (stated and demonstrated): another gate's work that O's block itself runs synchronously. Examples are a queue drained inline, a non-asyncio scheduler or uvloop driven inside the block, and finalizers or signal handlers that fire inside it.
designs.mechanism:
IDENTITY: at tracer __enter__, each resolved function F gets a _Swap in a process-wide registry. The _Swap holds original = F.__code__ and replica = original.replace(), which was tested to be a distinct, equal, behaviour-preserving object on 3.10–3.13. The tracer then sets F.__code__ = replica. The registry is reference-counted across nested and concurrent tracers, so any order of tracer exits restores correctly. At the last exit it restores F.__code__ = original, but only if F still holds the replica; otherwise it adds a CODE_REBOUND note and leaves F alone. Then one gc.get_referrers(*replicas) pass finds any function other than F that holds a replica, which is a fatal CODE_CLONED problem. Frames already running the replica finish normally.

OBSERVATION, 3.12+: sys.monitoring with tool id 4, or 3 if 4 is taken. The DEBUGGER, COVERAGE, PROFILER and OPTIMIZER ids are never taken; if 4 and 3 are both busy the tracer refuses MONITOR_BUSY. The only event is local PY_START, set on the replicas only. It fires in every thread (including pre-existing and _thread ones), costs nothing for any other code, and does not use setprofile or settrace at all. cProfile (which uses sys.monitoring on 3.12+), coverage, debuggers and a harness calling sys.setprofile all coexist with it. The callback gets the target frame as sys._getframe(1). Events are not re-entrant during a callback (tested). If the callback raises, the exception surfaces from the target call, the body does not run, and the local events remain set (tested). A tool freed or reset by someone else becomes a MONITOR_LOST note at exit.

OBSERVATION, 3.9–3.11: a per-thread _Hook installed with sys.setprofile. It is installed only when that thread's marker depth goes 0→1 (a section with-block entered on it, or a carried invocation starting on it) and removed at 1→0 in a finally block. threading.setprofile is never used.
- A pre-existing Python-level profiler is chained. A C-level profiler refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER before anything is touched (cProfile tested to be still installed and still recording).
- If CPython dropped the hook because an exception arose inside a profile function, the user's chained profiler is reinstalled and a HOOK_GONE note is recorded. If the harness replaced the profiler, the hook is marked dead and a PROFILER_REPLACED note is recorded.
- A section closed on a different thread marks that thread's hook dead; a dead hook removes itself on its next event.
- A fresh start is f_lasti == -1 (3.9/3.10) or the offset of RESUME 0 (3.11). Generator resumes are ignored, matching the PY_START semantics of 3.12+ (tested).

OBSERVER RULES, both backends: the callback reads id(code) → _Swap and checks `is`. It walks f_back and reads the marker dict without a lock; writers replace tuples rather than mutating them in place. It increments this thread's own count dict. It holds no lock at any point, so a finalizer that calls a target during record() cannot deadlock. Its only exception handler is `except BaseException: note; raise`, so a signal handler's exception is never swallowed. It never refuses.

LIFECYCLE:
- Entry order: resolve all targets → acquire the backend → swap codes.
- section() returns a single-use context manager that checks, in order: declared name, tracer active, with-form, not nested, then pushes its marker.
- carry(fn) returns a wrapper that pushes and pops its own frame as a marker for each invocation.
- Exit order: close any openings still open (an OPEN_AT_EXIT note), restore codes, run the clone scan, release the backend, and only then set complete=True. A crash inside exit therefore yields INCOMPLETE_TRACE.
- record() merges the per-thread counts into: tracer, gates_sha256, complete, backend, targets (sha256 of the original code, provenance only), provenance (module:qualname@file:line), sections (every opened section present even when empty), after_close, unattributed, dispatched, problems (fatal), notes (under-count diagnostics). score() and check_metrics() read problems and complete.
machinery_removed: _code_holders / _wrappers_of / _sharing_problem: gc.get_referrers holder and wrapper scans, run at entry and again at every section close, together with the per-close gc.collect() and the SHARED_CODE reason code
inspect.unwrap in _resolve_target: declared objects are never unwrapped
_identity and frame-identity matching: comparing f_globals with the declared globals and f_locals with closure cells (and the per-call f_locals cost), plus the 'impostors' bucket
_THREAD_START_CODE interception of threading.Thread.start, the _thread_section lineage map, THREAD_OUTLIVES, and the 'ambiguous' bucket with its only-one-open-section rule
the ContextVar section slot, token reset, and SECTION_CONTEXT

threading.setprofile everywhere, the per-tracer _Hook chain, _skip_exited self-removal chaining, EXIT_ORDER, _hook_chain_has_self, and the PROFILER_REPLACED refusal (on 3.9–3.11 it survives only as a non-fatal note)
the hook's `except Exception` and the sticky _hook_failed / HOOK_FAILED
the non-reentrant self._lock taken inside the hook
_refuse_at_close raising at section close, and the unread close_refusals list
sys.setprofile entirely on Python 3.12+
machinery_added: _Swap registry: one private replica per declared function object (fn.__code__ = fn.__code__.replace()), reference-counted across tracers, restored at the last exit
3.12+ backend: sys.monitoring tool id 4 or 3, with local PY_START events on the replicas only; MONITOR_BUSY at entry, MONITOR_LOST note at exit

3.9–3.11 backend: a per-thread sys.setprofile _Hook present only while that thread holds a marker, with a per-thread depth counter, a Python-profiler chain, restoration of a user profiler dropped by an exception, and a dead-flag for self-removal
a live-stack attribution walk: frame→opening marker dict, cut at asyncio.events.Handle._run, lock-free and non-swallowing observer, per-thread count dicts
a with-statement form check at section __enter__ (SETUP_WITH or BEFORE_WITH at the caller's f_lasti, cached per code object), with a hop through @contextlib.contextmanager helpers
cov.carry(fn): an explicit delegation API for threads, pools, executors and asyncio tasks (sync and coroutine functions)
record()['problems'] (fatal: every refusal raised at section or carry time is also written here, plus CODE_CLONED) and record()['notes'] (under-count diagnostics appended to NOT_EXERCISED)
record()['complete'], set last at exit, and the score-side INCOMPLETE_TRACE check
one gc.get_referrers pass over the replicas at tracer exit, giving CODE_CLONED
