diagnostic buckets 'dispatched', 'unattributed' and 'after_close', plus per-target provenance in the record

finding_closure.how: Identity is the declared function object's private replica, not a code object shared with others. Factory closures and no-wraps siblings run the original code, which is never observed. e2: entry_b is not credited for entry_a, make_scorer(abs,True) is not credited for score_lenient (NOT_EXERCISED), and the declared object itself passes. No other door exists: running the replica requires either calling F or reading F.__code__ during the trace (see R3-D1 and stated limit L4).

Lookup is by id(code) followed by `is` against a freshly created replica; equality is never consulted. e2: a vendored equal-code copy, an exec'd copy of the whole module and DB.__init__ versus DA.__init__ are all NOT_EXERCISED on 3.10–3.13.

There is no global, context or thread slot: credit comes only from a marker on the executing thread's live chain. e3: a thread started in A calling f while B is open credits neither; an unsectioned background thread during B credits nothing; tasks are cut at Handle._run.

On 3.12+ it is closed structurally: setprofile is never used, and cProfile (which uses sys.monitoring) coexists (e4: traced count 1, cProfile still recording). On 3.9–3.11 a C-level profiler refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER at section enter before anything is touched (e4: cProfile still installed, entries recorded). The refusal is also written to problems, so swallowing it still refuses at score (e7).

Tracers never chain each other's hooks. Code swaps are reference-counted in one registry, and there is one per-thread hook with a depth counter. e4: non-LIFO exits of two tracers on the same target leave both counted, the code restored, and no profiler or thread profiler behind. Re-entering a tracer or section refuses REENTRY (a kept patch).

The catch-all remains: any exception during import or attribute access becomes [V5:UNRESOLVED]. The __wrapped__ loop case is gone because nothing is unwrapped. e2: a nonexistent module gives UNRESOLVED.

The string-key checks are kept and extended to the new problems list. e6: int or None keys in targets, sections or inside a section, a list-valued section and a non-list problems all give BAD_TRACE; a bool count or a forged undeclared key gives BAD_COUNT.

Parallel sections in two threads and _thread-started threads now work: sections by the live stack, _thread work via carry (e3, e7). A harness setprofile inside a section no longer blinds tracing on 3.12+; on 3.9–3.11 it is an under-count note. The remaining over-blocking is published in over_blocking_costs: uncarried concurrency, pre-existing threads, non-function targets, section form, and C profilers on 3.9–3.11.

The class-own-__dict__ rule (INHERITED) and _TARGET_RE.fullmatch are kept. e2: Sub.fit gives INHERITED; a trailing newline gives DECL. Base.fit is credited when Other().fit() runs, because that IS Base.fit (object identity).

Runtime decoration builds a new function from the decorator's original inner code, which is never the replica. e2: timed(cheap_path)() is not credited as score_all. No check at close is needed because there is no sharing to recount.

Pool threads are never credited through lineage. A carried job credits exactly the opening it was carried from, whichever thread created the pool. e3: with A and B open concurrently on a shared pool, uncarried work credits neither and a carried job credits B {f:1} only (exact counts in e3b).

threading.setprofile is never used. On 3.9–3.11 a thread has a hook only while it holds a marker, and it is removed in a finally block (or self-removes if dead). e4: threads and _thread threads started inside a section see sys.getprofile() and the thread profiler as None.

INSTANCE_PATH is kept for attributes an instance gets from its class (e9: holder.method refused). It is relaxed only for the instance's own __dict__ slots, where no MRO is involved (holder.handler and SimpleNamespace resolve).
There is no unwrapping: a declared wraps wrapper is its own object with its own replica. e2: run_safe is not credited for run_fast; run_fast itself passes.

One pool used across sequential sections, multiprocessing ThreadPool (terminate without join), run_in_executor and to_thread all score when their jobs are carried (e3). THREAD_OUTLIVES no longer exists. Executor or thread work that is not carried is refused NOT_EXERCISED, with the 'unattributed' and 'dispatched' diagnostics; this is published.

No refusal depends on the observer's health; a missed observation can only under-count, never produce a wrong-reason refusal. e4: recursion to the limit inside a section scores PASS with notes CALLBACK_RAISED and HOOK_GONE (3.9–3.11 only), and no profiler is left on any version.

There is no threading hook to leak. The per-thread hook is uninstalled in the finally of every marker extent; exception exits and non-LIFO exits were tested with nothing left behind (e3/e4 print 'profile left: None').

The foreign-context-exit escape cannot occur because no ContextVar is used, and section __exit__ never raises. check_metrics on a non-dict keeps its round-3 report-not-raise patch. The prototype check() returns NO_TRACE for a non-dict.

Products of make_mul(3) run the lambda code from make_mul's co_consts, never double's replica. e2: make_mul(3)(5) is NOT_EXERCISED for declared double, P2 (same closure, other default) is NOT_EXERCISED, and double(5) passes.

Contexts are never read, and task chains are cut at Handle._run. e3, e3b: in the t12 shape (consumer tasks created lazily in A run B's f while both are open) A is not credited (A={}, dispatched {f:1}). In the sync-driven cross-thread variant neither is credited. With B's job carried, B is credited and A is not.
The observer's only handler is `except BaseException: note; raise`. e4: a SIGALRM Timeout was delivered 20/20 on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, versus 4–10 of 20 under the round-3 implementation.

Object identity with no unwrapping. T01a: a plain caller of _run is not credited for run_fast. T01b: a class-based update_wrapper declaration refuses NO_CODE (a disclosed over-block). T01c: a per-call wraps sibling is not credited. T01d: an undecorated score with two wraps aliases is accepted, credited when an alias calls score. All in e2 on 3.10–3.13.

There are no close-time refusals. Every refusal raised at section or carry time is also appended to record()['problems'], which score() reads. e3/e7: a swallowed NESTED_SECTION, SECTION_FORM (ExitStack), CARRY_OUTSIDE or FOREIGN_PROFILER still refuses at score with its own code, and a section exiting by exception still credits the calls made before it.

The observer takes no lock; counts go into per-thread dicts, and record() only copies them. e4: at gc threshold 5, 20k cyclic objects whose __del__ calls the target, with record() called every 50 iterations, completed on 3.10–3.13 with no hang.

Section close does no gc and no heap scan. e5: 1000 section open/close pairs take 5–18 ms in total. One gc.get_referrers pass per tracer exit takes 75–90 ms on a 3M-object heap; entry takes about 1 ms for 18 targets.

THREAD_OUTLIVES is gone: a thread that is never carried is simply never credited, so it cannot make a section refuse. e3: a daemon thread started in a section and never joined, with the section's own call, scores PASS.

Two concurrent shards with the same section name each credit their own opening, merged under the one name (e3: A={f:1, g:1}, PASS). A singledispatch entry point resolves to its dispatch wrapper function and is credited when called (e2 PASS).

An instance step is allowed when the attribute is in that object's own __dict__ (e2: registry.handler PASS; e9: holder.handler PASS). The INSTANCE_PATH message now says the attribute comes from the class.
getattr is used as a fallback only when the module defines __getattr__ (e9: fxlazy:lazy_fn PASS). Whatever object it returns at trace entry is the declared object.
There is no hook_failed state. Observer failures are counted as CALLBACK_RAISED notes for the tracer that was active, and are non-fatal.

On 3.9–3.11, a hook dropped by CPython gets the user's profiler reinstalled at the end of the marker extent (e4: user profiler kept 10/10 on 3.10 and 3.11). On 3.12+ styxx is not in the setprofile chain. The residual losses seen there (1–4 of 10) are baseline CPython: the control e4b loses the profiler in 6–13 of 20 with no tracer at all.

f_locals is never read, since there is no closure-cell identity check. The cost per target start is +1.4–2.3 µs at shallow depth and grows with stack depth instead (+19–28 µs at depth 200); this is published.
No ContextVar exists. A marker lives exactly as long as its with-block, or its carry invocation.

Clones share the original code and are never credited, whatever their cells or defaults. The only exception is an in-trace clone of the replica itself (stated limit L4; detected if still alive at exit, e2 CODE_CLONED).

over_blocking_costs: Concurrency must be carried. Work run on threads, ThreadPoolExecutor or ThreadPool workers, run_in_executor/to_thread, or asyncio tasks (gather, create_task, TaskGroup, and wait_for on ≤3.11, which wraps its argument in a task) counts only inside cov.carry(fn). Uncarried, it is refused NOT_EXERCISED with 'unattributed' or 'dispatched' diagnostics. The round-2/3 valid cases 'thread started in section', 'pool created and shut down in section' and 'task created and awaited in section' therefore need carry, which means a new exam prereg.
A sync section that drives asyncio (asyncio.run(main()) inside `with section`) credits nothing unless main is carried: asyncio.run(cov.carry(main)()). Each child task main spawns needs its own carry.
Child processes and process pools are never observed, and a carried wrapper is not picklable.

Only plain Python functions can be declared. lru_cache/cache-decorated entry points, functools.partial, callable instances, class-based wrappers, property, singledispatchmethod, bound methods and Cython/numba functions refuse NO_CODE. Nothing is unwrapped, so a call made directly to __wrapped__ does not count for the wrapper.

section() must be entered by a literal `with` statement, optionally through @contextlib.contextmanager helpers. ExitStack.enter_context, pytest fixtures, a manual __enter__ and asynccontextmanager helpers refuse SECTION_FORM at open.

Once raised at section or carry time, NESTED_SECTION, SECTION_FORM, UNDECLARED_SECTION (for that name), CARRY_OUTSIDE and FOREIGN_PROFILER refuse the named section's gates at score, even if the harness caught the error and recovered.
On 3.9–3.11, a C-level profiler (cProfile, yappi, line_profiler) on the thread where a section opens or a carried job runs refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER. There is no such refusal on 3.12+.

On 3.9–3.11, pure-Python code inside an open section runs about 10–11x slower (a profile hook on every event on that thread). Outside sections and on other threads it runs at about 1.0x. On 3.12+ it is about 1.0x everywhere.
Every start of a target costs a stack walk: +1.4–2.3 µs at shallow depth, +19–28 µs at depth 200. A deeply recursive declared target that is called very often pays O(depth) per call.

Tools keyed on code-object identity (line_profiler, code-identity memoisation, some JIT caches) do not recognise the declared functions during the trace. inspect.signature, getsource and pickling are unchanged (e7).
Not counted: a call already running when the trace begins, a generator created from the target before the trace, and function objects created by an importlib.reload during the trace.
Functions executed only from inside the observer callback (styxx's own _on_start) can never be declared (e6: GX refused).
On 3.12+, MONITOR_BUSY refuses if another component holds both sys.monitoring tool ids 3 and 4.
On 3.9–3.11 only, a section opened inside a generator that is resumed on another thread under-counts (SECTION_THREAD note).
On 3.9–3.11, the 'unattributed' diagnostic covers only threads that hold a marker, so a NOT_EXERCISED message can tell less about where calls went than it does on 3.12+.
Each tracer exit makes one heap scan for CODE_CLONED, about 75–90 ms at 3M objects.
stated_limits: Exercised is not tested (carried forward): one call whose result is discarded satisfies a declaration.
Transitive calls count (carried forward): a target reached through another function counts, so order_stat_bar via reachable(n_draws>1) satisfies P1's G1.
The trace is written by the runner (carried forward): forgery is an accepted residual. The threat model is honest-but-careless authors.
Only declared gates are checked (carried forward). G3's hard-coded baseline is out of scope.

L1 (attribution residual, demonstrated in e8): work belonging to another gate that O's with-block itself runs synchronously counts for O. Examples: a queue of B's jobs drained inline in A, or a generator created elsewhere and advanced in A. The stack shows who is waiting on a call, not who asked for it.

L2 (demonstrated in e8): only asyncio's Handle._run is recognised as a dispatch boundary. A hand-rolled scheduler, trio/curio, or uvloop (Cython handles) driven inside a section credits the tasks it runs to that section.
L3 (demonstrated in e8): finalizers (__del__, weakref callbacks) and signal handlers that fire inside a section's extent are credited to it.

L4 (demonstrated in e8): a function built from the declared function's __code__ during the trace runs as the declared function. This covers types.FunctionType(f.__code__, ...), g.__code__ = f.__code__ and exec(f.__code__). It is detected (CODE_CLONED) only if still alive at trace exit. It requires reading f.__code__ deliberately.

L5 (demonstrated in e8): the declared object is whatever the name is bound to at trace entry. A mock installed before the trace is what gets checked. Provenance (module:qualname@file:line) is recorded for a reader, not verified.
carry() is an assertion by the author: a carried callable counts for the section it was carried from, wherever it runs.
Rebinding a declared function's __code__ during the trace (e.g. an IPython autoreload) makes later calls unobserved. That under-counts and is noted as CODE_REBOUND.
Python 3.9 is untested (no interpreter available). Free-threaded builds are untested; F.__code__ assignment racing with concurrent calls is the main concern there.
The with-statement opcode check covers SETUP_WITH (3.9/3.10) and BEFORE_WITH (3.11–3.13). Python 3.14 replaces BEFORE_WITH, so the check must be extended before 3.14 is supported.

claims_that_do_not_hold: R1-B3 / R3-B2 CLOSED_STRUCTURALLY ('concurrent sections cannot cross-credit'): this fails when work is submitted from another thread into an event loop that runs inside another section's cov.run. In judge1/n_attacks.py X2, A = cov.run('A', asyncio.run, main_a()), where main_a never calls f. B, open at the same time on another thread, calls run_coroutine_threadsafe(job_b(), loopA). A is credited f:1 and scores PASS on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13. The attribution text says the loop's tasks are 'inside that section by definition', but B's work being credited to A is exactly the R3-B2 outcome.

R3-B2 ('tasks opening their own run_async sections are attributed exactly'): the design's own remedy is to give each worker or task its own section. Doing that on a long-lived consumer brings the t12 false pass back. In X4, A's consumer thread opens its own 'A' opening and drains a queue, B enqueues jmod.f, and A PASSes with f:1 on 3.10–3.13. stated_limits discloses only generators and coroutines resumed in another section, not queue drains or sectioned consumers.

e2's 'module attribute rebound to a mock -> NOT_EXERCISED' covers only rebinding during the trace. A stub function bound at the declared name before the trace (e.g. a fixture's monkeypatch) is itself resolved, minted and credited. X1 PASSes, with provenance pointing at jstub.py and nothing checking it. This limit is not listed.
holes_found: X2: a concurrently open section B submits work cross-thread (run_coroutine_threadsafe / call_soon_threadsafe) into a loop running inside cov.run('A', ...), and A is credited for it. Verified on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13. The Handle._run cut graft closes it.
X4: a consumer that opened its own opening of section A executes jobs B enqueued, and A is credited. This is the 'where, not who' residual, and it is not stated.
X1: a stub bound at the declared path before the trace is the declared target, and is credited. Common to all three designs.
Stated, confirmed: a same-globals clone built in-trace from T.__code__ and dropped before exit is credited. Code injected onto the section's stack (signal handlers, finalizers) counts.

Minor: open-time refusals (NESTED_SECTION, FOREIGN_PROFILER, UNDECLARED_SECTION) are raised but not recorded in the trace. I found no false pass from this, because the section never opens, but the swallowed-refusal audit trail is weaker than v5m's.
per_design.summary: This has the strongest identity rule of the three. A frame counts only if its f_code is a minted code object M_T and its f_globals is T.__globals__, with CLONE_CALLED, CLONE_ALIVE and CODE_SWAPPED tripwires. None of my identity attacks, and none of the round 1–3 class-A cases, got through except the stated in-trace clone. Attribution uses the fewest moving parts: a registered anchor frame on the live f_back chain, with no ContextVar, no inheritance and no CPython-internal interception. The unmodified P1 retro is exact: I re-ran it and got {reachable: 12} plus NOT_EXERCISED naming exactly the other four. I found two false passes it did not state. X2 (a cross-thread job credited to a section whose stack runs the loop) is closed by a one-line graft, which I verified in scratch. X4 (sectioned shared consumers) is the universal where-not-who residual and needs stating. It over-blocks heavily: off-stack work never counts, sections must be calls, a raised section refuses, hook loss from signals or RecursionError refuses, and foreign profilers are refused on <=3.11. Most of those refusals only guard against under-counting and can be demoted to notes at no soundness cost.

per_design.name: v5e "lower-bound trace": one-owner carriers for identity, opener-stack ownership for attribution
claims_that_do_not_hold: R3-B2 CLOSED_STRUCTURALLY and R2-B2 CLOSED_STRUCTURALLY: a timing variant of t12 passes. Section A starts a plain consumer thread (X5) or task (X5b), which inherits A. B enqueues jmod.f fire-and-forget and closes. The job runs while A is the only open instance, so the INHERITED call is credited to A. A scores PASS with f:1 on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13, and A's author did nothing explicit. The stated limit covers only producers 'outside every section'; here the producer is section B.

'WHY THE CLASS CANNOT REOPEN ... every class-B door from the three rounds is an instance of one of these [three impossibilities]': R3-B2 (A credited for B's job run on A's inherited consumer) is not one of the three. It reopens because exclusivity is judged when the call runs, not when the job is submitted.

R3-D1 closure relies on 'run_fast is its own carrier'. For an ordinary nested @functools.wraps decorator, though, the carrier is the inner function. A harness calling entry.__wrapped__(x), bypassing the wrapper's validation (X7), or lru_cache's __wrapped__ (X8) is credited as the declared entry point. This is stated as a limit, but it means the declared wrapper is never actually verified to run.
holes_found: X5/X5b: a fire-and-forget job from B, executed by A's inherited worker thread or asyncio consumer task after B closes, is credited to A. Undisclosed; verified on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13.
X7/X8: calling __wrapped__ credits the declared decorated target, including lru_cache. Stated.
X1: a stub bound before the trace is accepted, because a module-level def in a test file is non-CO_NESTED and the sole holder. Undisclosed.
Stated: on 3.10, exec(f.__code__) and generators of freed clones are credited. Unsectioned producers feeding a sole-open section's workers are credited.

Structural fragility: correctness rests on concurrent.futures._WorkItem internals (gone in 3.14), Thread.start f_locals interception, ContextVar agreement, and gc-visibility of holders. Each is a heuristic door of the kind rounds 1–3 kept reopening.
per_design.summary: This design has the broadest honest-harness coverage for sequential sections: with-sections, pools, tasks and executors reused across sections, lru_cache, and raised sections. It gets that breadth by keeping inheritance: a time-window exclusivity rule plus ContextVar, Thread.start and _WorkItem provenance. That is exactly the machinery rounds 1–3 kept breaking, and I reopened R3-B2 with a timing change: B leaves before its job runs on A's inherited consumer, and A passes. Its identity rule defines a decorated target as its inner body, so calls through __wrapped__ count. It also over-blocks targets the minting designs handle soundly: factory products, closures, dataclass methods and singledispatch. It has the most machinery and the weakest soundness under this lens.

per_design.name: v5m: private replica + live stack
claims_that_do_not_hold: R2-B2 / R3-B2 CLOSED_STRUCTURALLY: this holds only for uncarried work. carry() is the documented remedy for every thread, pool and task, and applying it brings the false pass back. In X3b, A's carried consumer thread runs B's queued job and A PASSes. In X3, a cov.carry() wrapper created lazily in A and cached is invoked synchronously inside B's own with-block. It credits A and not B, silently, because carried frames get no nesting check and the nearest marker wins. Verified on 3.11 and 3.12. This is disclosed only generically ('carry() is an assertion by the author').

R1-B1 'no other door exists': true only as a statement about who can reach the replica. exec(jmod.f.__code__, {}) inside a section is credited as f, with no tripwire (X5, 3.11 and 3.12). It is listed under L4, but there is no CLONE_CALLED-style check of f_globals, as the mint-and-anchor design has.
holes_found: X3: a cached carry() wrapper from section A, called on B's with-block stack while both are open, credits A and not B. No refusal. Undisclosed in this specific form.
X3b: a carried long-lived consumer credits its section for other gates' jobs (the where-not-who residual via carry).
X5: bare exec of the replica under foreign globals is credited (stated L4, not detected).
X1: a stub bound before the trace is credited (stated L5).
Stated: L1 inline queue drain, L2 non-asyncio schedulers and uvloop run inside a section, L3 finalizers and signals.

Fragility: the SECTION_FORM check depends on the SETUP_WITH/BEFORE_WITH opcode at f_lasti, which must change for 3.14. There are two observation backends (sys.monitoring on 3.12+, scoped setprofile on <=3.11) that must be proven equivalent.
per_design.summary: Its identity rule is the same sound minting idea as mint-and-anchor, minus the f_globals tripwire. The Handle._run dispatch cut is the right idea: it closes the cross-thread loop-submission door that mint-and-anchor leaves open (X2 gives A nothing here). Recording refusals into problems and demoting hook mishaps to notes are good lower-bound mechanics, and sys.monitoring on 3.12+ removes most profiler over-blocking. carry() is its weak point. It is the only way to count concurrent work, and it attaches a section label to a callable that then credits that section wherever and on whoever's stack it runs, with no nesting check. So the careless shared-helper and shared-consumer shapes re-create R2-B2 and R3-B2. With-form opcode inspection and dual backends cost simplicity and testability. It comes a close second, and it is the main graft donor.

judge:1.winner: v5e "mint-and-anchor": the narrowest sound coverage instrument
grafts: From v5m: stop the attribution f_back walk, and the NESTED_SECTION walk, at asyncio.events.Handle._run, the loop dispatch boundary. This closes X2 (B's cross-thread job credited to a section running the loop); verified in scratch on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13, where X2 then refuses NOT_EXERCISED for A and asyncio.run(cov.run_async('G', main)) still counts. It also lets tasks inside such a loop open their own sections instead of refusing NESTED_SECTION. Document that cov.run(name, asyncio.run, main()) counts nothing and asyncio.run(cov.run_async(...)) is the form to use.

NEW (none of the three has it): a provenance gate at resolution. Refuse [V5:FOREIGN_DEFINITION] when the resolved function's __module__ is not the declared module. This closes X1, the stub bound at the declared name by a fixture before the trace, which all three designs credit. Verified: all five P1 targets have __module__ 'styxx.power', so the retro is unaffected. wraps wrappers copy __module__ and still pass.

From v5m: write open-time refusals (NESTED_SECTION, FOREIGN_PROFILER, UNDECLARED_SECTION, TRACE_INACTIVE) into the trace as well as raising them, so a harness that swallows one still refuses at score.

From v5m / lower-bound: demote findings that can only lose calls to notes. That means PROFILER_LOST, THREAD_HOP, OPEN_AT_EXIT and end=='raised' (SECTION_UNFINISHED). No credit is possible without a registered open anchor on the live chain, so these refusals only over-block (pytest-timeout's signal method, recursion-limit batteries, sections that raise as expected). Keep CODE_SWAPPED, CLONE_ALIVE and CLONE_CALLED as refusals: a __code__ swapped to another target's minted code could over-credit.

From v5m (optional, 3.12+ only): observe with sys.monitoring local PY_START on the minted code objects instead of setprofile. Attribution stays identical, and it removes FOREIGN_PROFILER and hook-loss on 3.12+ along with the per-event cost. Adopt only if both backends run the same e2/e3 batteries byte-identically.

From v5m L1 and the lower-bound design's 'where not who' limit: state explicitly that a section's own stack, or a worker that opened an opening of that section name, which drains another gate's queued jobs is credited for them (X4). Keep the current NESTED_SECTION refusal, which makes a job wrapped in B's section fail closed on A's consumer (X4b).
judge:1.rationale:
I judged soundness first. I attacked all three prototypes with scratch harnesses in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1230efe6-3e44-5eb6-ad91-35910fea5db9/scratchpad/design/judge1/ (n_attacks.py, m_attacks.py, r_attacks.py, n_graft.py, with fixtures jmod.py, jstub.py and jdeco.py). I re-ran each P1 retro, and all three are exact.

For identity (class A), the two minting designs are the sound ones. A minted code object reaches a frame only by calling T or by deliberately reading T.__code__ during the trace. None of my attacks, and none of the round 1–3 cases, got past minting. mint-and-anchor adds the f_globals identity tripwire (CLONE_CALLED), which v5m lacks: exec(f.__code__, {}) is credited silently under v5m (X5). The lower-bound design defines a decorated target as its inner body, so __wrapped__ calls are credited (X7, X8), and it refuses closures and factories that minting handles soundly.

For attribution (class B), the lower-bound design keeps inheritance and a time-window exclusivity rule. I reopened R3-B2 with a timing change: B enqueues a job fire-and-forget and closes, the job runs on A's inherited worker or task, and A passes on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13 with no explicit act by A's author. That design claims the case is CLOSED_STRUCTURALLY and does not disclose this. v5m's Handle._run cut is correct, but carry() re-creates cross-section credit silently. A cached carried helper invoked on B's own with-block stack credits A (X3), and there is no nesting check.

mint-and-anchor attributes only by a registered anchor frame on the live f_back chain. Of the three it has the least machinery and the fewest heuristics: no ContextVar, no Thread.start or _WorkItem interception, no gc scans, one hook with no try/except. Its equivalent of X3 (a callable labelled with section A, invoked inside B) fails closed with NESTED_SECTION (X4b). Its one false pass that is neither stated nor shared by all three is X2, B's cross-thread submission into a loop running inside A. The Handle._run graft from v5m closes it, verified in scratch on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13 with the async control still passing. The pre-trace stub door (X1) is common to all three; a __module__ provenance graft closes it without touching the P1 retro. The remaining shared residual is the where-not-who queue-drain (X4), which only needs stating.

mint-and-anchor's cost is over-blocking. Most of it (PROFILER_LOST, THREAD_HOP, SECTION_UNFINISHED) guards only against under-counting and can be demoted to notes, as v5m and the lower-bound design do, with no loss of soundness. Its single backend and one-sentence rules also make it the most testable. With the listed grafts it is the design least likely to be re-entered through another door in round 4.

per_design.name: v5e "mint-and-anchor": the narrowest sound coverage instrument
claims_that_do_not_hold: R1-B3 / R3-B2 CLOSED_STRUCTURALLY, and the attribution claims 'asyncio Task, loop callback ... cannot reach a section's anchor' and 'Concurrent sections cannot cross-credit'. Neither holds once an event loop runs inside a section. Test (judge2/probe_narrow2.py): cov.run('A', <runs loop.run_until_complete>) on thread 1, and on thread 2 cov.run('B', ...) submits job() via run_coroutine_threadsafe. Result: gate A VERDICT PASS {'jfx:target': 1}, although A's own code never calls target (3.11 and 3.12). The WHY text says the loop's tasks are 'inside that section by definition', and that definition is exactly the cross-credit.

The stated limits leave out the queue-drain shape: A's stack runs a job that B's section queued, and A gets the credit. Test: gate A VERDICT PASS while A never names target (probe_narrow2.py P2iso). v5m (L1) and lower-bound state this limit. This design does not, and claims no cross-credit instead.

R2-D4 and R3-B3 are called closed, but refusing PROFILER_LOST is a new over-block, and a nondeterministic one. Losing the hook can only drop calls, so the refusal adds no soundness. Test (probe_flaky.py): a battery calls the target and then catches a SIGALRM Timeout in a solver loop. Across 20 runs of the identical harness it refused PROFILER_LOST 12 times on 3.11 and 17 times on 3.13, and scored PASS otherwise. A caught RecursionError after the target was called also refuses (probe_narrow.py P3).

R3-D2 CLOSED_STRUCTURALLY via SECTION_UNFINISHED. Refusing a raised opening is over-blocking, not a closure. Calls made before the raise are real, and close already runs on both paths. Test: the honest per-case refusal battery `try: cov.run('G', refuses, x) except PowerError` refuses SECTION_UNFINISHED (P4) with every target called. v5m and lower-bound both score the same shape.
holes_found: A cross-thread job submitted onto an event loop that runs inside another section's cov.run is credited to that section (false PASS, demonstrated on 3.11 and 3.12).
An inline drain of another section's queued jobs is credited to the section doing the draining (false PASS, demonstrated). It is not disclosed.
Stated residual: a clone built during the trace with T's own globals and dropped before exit is credited.
per_design.summary: The best adoption-to-soundness ratio. One setprofile backend, about 300 LOC, and byte-identical battery outputs on 3.10–3.13. Both rules are facts about the stack or about object identity, so every rule can be pinned by a deterministic mutant; PROFILER_LOST can be forced with sys.setprofile(None) in fn. Minting accepts the widest set of honest targets: factory products, no-wraps decorator products, dataclass methods and singledispatch. The f_globals CLONE_CALLED tripwire gives it the strongest identity of the three. The P1 retro is exact with run_p1 unmodified (reproduced on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13); only the exam runner changes to cov.run. Its over-blocking comes mostly from refusals that buy no soundness: PROFILER_LOST, which is flaky under signals; SECTION_UNFINISHED, which refuses expected-exception batteries; and ALIAS, THREAD_HOP and CODE_SWAPPED. It also refuses every foreign setprofile profiler, including pure-Python ones. The NOT_EXERCISED message says 'never executed' for targets that did run on pool threads or child tasks (P5/P6), which misleads honest authors. The one demonstrated false pass is the where-not-who class (a loop or queue drained inside a section), and the claims overstate closure there.

per_design.name: v5e "lower-bound trace": one-owner carriers for identity, opener-stack ownership for attribution
claims_that_do_not_hold: The attribution WHY lists 'a unit descended from no section credits the open section' among the things that cannot happen. The design's own stated limit and e8 show an unsectioned producer feeding G's worker scoring for G. The guarantee is about units, not work, so the class-B door is admitted rather than closed.

R2-D3 and R1-D4: 'sequential shapes now score' holds only if no other section is open at call time. The same harness flips verdict with scheduling (probe_lb.py): G's pool jobs with H opening at t=0 give NOT_EXERCISED with ambiguous {'jfx:target': 2}; with H opening after G closes, the same code scores PASS (3.11 and 3.12). This verdict flakiness is not disclosed as such.

R2-B1 is presented as closed ('cannot be declared at all'), but for honest code it is an unfixable over-block. `@timed def score_all` (a decorator without wraps) refuses NESTED_CODE, and the inner function is bound to no name, so the entry point cannot be declared without editing the code under test. Factory products (double = make_mul(2)) and dataclass __init__ also refuse NESTED_CODE; singledispatch refuses SHARED_ROUTE (all demonstrated).
R1-B1 is called CLOSED_STRUCTURALLY, yet on 3.9/3.10 exec(carrier.__code__) and a generator from a dead clone are credited, by the design's own stated limit. So it is structural only on 3.11+.
holes_found: While G is the only open section, work that unsectioned code feeds into G's inherited workers is credited to G (stated; tested by the designer to score).
An inline drain of another section's jobs is credited to the section doing the draining (demonstrated PASS; stated).
A call through entry.__wrapped__ credits the declared wrapper (stated).
3.10: bare exec of the carrier's code is credited (stated).
per_design.summary: The broadest attribution for honest harnesses: with-blocks including ExitStack, @contextmanager and fixtures; pools, tasks and executors when sections do not overlap; exceptions tolerated; hook mishaps kept as notes; lru_cache accepted. The principle that counts are lower bounds is right, and the other designs should take it. The cost is the highest complexity of the three: CO_NESTED carrier selection, the gc-graph SHARED_ROUTE analysis (which differs by version; the designer found a 3.10 door in their own draft), heap scans inside the hook on the first credited call, private concurrent.futures._WorkItem internals that break on 3.14, Thread.start interception, a ContextVar, contextlib opener heuristics, and a busy set. Credit depends on thread timing through the exclusivity rule, so a frozen exam cannot pin it deterministically and honest verdicts can be flaky. Identity over-blocks common research-code shapes (no-wraps decorators, factories, dataclasses) with no remedy short of editing the module under test. The P1 retro is exact (reproduced on all four versions).

per_design.name: v5m: private replica + live stack
claims_that_do_not_hold: R2-B2 and the WHY 'the only ways to be credited to O are to be synchronously awaited by O's with-block, or by a frame the author explicitly carried to O'. Because the nearest marker wins, a carried callback fired from B's with-block credits A, not B. Test (probe_v5m.py V1): A carries a callback into a shared registry, and B's section fires it while A is open. Result: gate A PASS {'jfx:target': 1}, and A's own flow never ran the target (3.11 and 3.12). carry() turns a careless registry into a cross-credit.

The experiments claim e10 (a helper inside a helper scores; ExitStack gives SECTION_FORM) is in the final regression log. final_all_versions.txt is truncated by a BrokenPipeError from `head` at e10 on 3.10 and 3.11, so those lines are missing. I reproduced ExitStack giving SECTION_FORM independently.
holes_found: A carried callback invoked from another section's flow credits the section that carried it (false PASS, demonstrated).

An in-trace clone with OTHER globals (FunctionType(f.__code__, {})), called and dropped, is credited: PASS, demonstrated V3. There is no f_globals check; mint catches this as CLONE_CALLED. L4 discloses it only in general terms.
An inline drain of another gate's jobs is credited (stated L1; demonstrated). Stated L2: non-asyncio schedulers are credited too.
per_design.summary: The same identity core as mint, the private replica, which reaches the P1 retro exactly (reproduced on all four versions). It has the soundest attribution against loops: the Handle._run cut correctly refuses the cross-thread-onto-loop case that fools mint. Hook mishaps and exceptions are notes, and per-case expected-exception batteries score. It accepts aliases, instance own-dict paths and PEP 562. On 3.12+ the sys.monitoring local-PY_START backend coexists with cProfile and setprofile tools at about 1.0x overhead, which is valuable. For adoption and testability it costs more: two backends with version-conditional expected outcomes (FOREIGN_PROFILER, HOOK_GONE and SECTION_THREAD exist only on ≤3.11), so an exam must run and mutate on both sides. There is a bytecode f_lasti check for the with-statement form that 3.14 breaks, and generator-start detection by RESUME offset on 3.11. carry() is an author-assertion door. Every thread, pool job and asyncio child task must be carried: `with section: asyncio.run(main())` credits nothing (V2), and gather needs a carry per coroutine. Fixtures and ExitStack are refused (SECTION_FORM). Code inside sections runs 10–11x slower on ≤3.11.

judge:2.winner: v5e "mint-and-anchor": the narrowest sound coverage instrument
grafts: From lower-bound (and v5m): COUNTS ARE LOWER BOUNDS. Demote every condition that can only lose calls to a note printed in the NOT_EXERCISED message: PROFILER_LOST, THREAD_HOP, CODE_SWAPPED, OPEN_AT_EXIT and end=='raised'. Keep the calls credited to a raised opening. Refuse only on over-credit tripwires (CLONE_ALIVE, CLONE_CALLED), malformed or stale traces, and missing targets. This removes the nondeterministic signal-timeout refusals (12/20 on 3.11, 17/20 on 3.13 in probe_flaky.py) and the per-case expected-exception over-block (P4), and cuts about five reason codes from the exam.

From v5m: resolution relaxations that stay sound under object identity, because the object is pinned at trace entry. Allow steps through an instance's own __dict__ (SimpleNamespace, registries) and the PEP 562 module __getattr__ fallback. Accept aliases, so one mint credits every declared name of that one object, instead of refusing ALIAS.

From v5m and lower-bound: diagnostic buckets. Count M_T hits on hooked threads that have no anchor on the chain (child tasks, callbacks) and hits after close. The NOT_EXERCISED message should name them and say that work on other threads, pools or tasks is never credited and must open its own cov.run or run_async. Today mint prints 'never executed' for targets that ran on a pool thread or a task (P5/P6).

From v5m, as a conditional graft: the asyncio Handle._run walk boundary. Adopting it closes the demonstrated loop-inside-section cross-credit, at the cost of asyncio.run inside cov.run crediting only through run_async. Under the adoption lens, the preferred alternative is to keep the breadth. Then add 'a scheduler or queue drained on a section's stack (an asyncio loop run inside cov.run, a queue of other sections' jobs) credits that section' to stated_limits, correct the R1-B3/R3-B2 claims, and freeze an exam case that pins the documented outcome.

From v5m, optional and only with a split exam: on 3.12+, observe minted code objects with sys.monitoring local PY_START events instead of setprofile. This drops FOREIGN_PROFILER on 3.12+, lets cProfile and pure-Python profilers coexist, gives about 1.0x overhead outside targets, and lets the diagnostic bucket see every thread. Keep the one setprofile backend if the exam cannot be run and mutated on both backends.

From lower-bound: accept C caching wrappers (lru_cache/cache) by minting their one-hop __wrapped__ FunctionType. Misses count and hits do not; disclose that a direct __wrapped__ call counts. Keep class-based wrappers, partial and property refused.

From lower-bound: exam hygiene. Pair every hazard sweep with a mutant that proves the sweep detects the defect, following the e7_mutant pattern (a record() holding the lock without the busy mark hangs at k=10..12). Keep the GC-threshold sweep for finalizer re-entry around open, close and record.
judge:2.rationale:
I judged on adoption and testability. All three designs reproduce the P1 retro exactly with run_p1.py unmodified on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13: {styxx.power:reachable: 12}, refusing [V5:NOT_EXERCISED] with exactly the other four named. So the retro does not separate them.

**Why mint-and-anchor wins.** It is the only design whose every rule is a fact about identity or stack structure, running on one observation backend. Its batteries are byte-identical across all four versions, so a frozen mutant exam can pin each rule deterministically.

- **Identity.** Minting accepts the widest set of honest targets: factory products, no-wraps decorator products, dataclass methods and singledispatch. The lower-bound design refuses most of these with no remedy short of editing the module under test. Mint also has the strongest identity tripwires; the CLONE_CALLED check catches an other-globals clone that v5m credits.
- **Over-blocking.** Most of mint's over-blocking comes from refusals that add no soundness: PROFILER_LOST, SECTION_UNFINISHED and ALIAS. Hook loss or a raise can only drop calls, never over-credit. I showed two costs of these refusals:
  - PROFILER_LOST makes an honest signal-timeout battery flaky: the same harness refused 12/20 runs on 3.11 and 17/20 on 3.13.
  - SECTION_UNFINISHED refuses per-case expected-refusal batteries, the natural shape for a 'refuses degenerate' gate.

  The lower-bound principle, where only over-credit refuses and everything else is a note, removes both costs cheaply.
- **Holes.** Mint's one demonstrated false pass is in the where-not-who class: an event loop run inside section A executes B's cross-thread job, or A drains B's queue, and A is credited. All three designs admit the queue form, but mint claimed closure there instead of disclosing it. That needs a claim correction plus either a stated limit or v5m's Handle._run cut.

**v5m is a close second.** It uses the same replica identity and has the soundest attribution against event loops. Its 3.12+ sys.monitoring backend is attractive. Against it:
- Two backends, a bytecode with-form check that 3.14 breaks, and version-conditional expected outcomes roughly double the exam matrix.
- carry() is an author-assertion door. I demonstrated a false PASS when a carried callback is fired from another section's flow.
- Async harnesses must carry every task.

**The lower-bound design has the broadest attribution** for pools, tasks and fixtures, and the right 'lower bound' principle. It ranks last under this lens:
- Its verdicts depend on thread scheduling through the exclusivity rule. I showed the same harness flipping between NOT_EXERCISED and PASS.
- Identity refuses common research-code entry points with no remedy.
- It rests on CO_NESTED, gc-graph SHARED_ROUTE analysis, private concurrent.futures internals and a busy set. This machinery is hard to freeze an exhaustive exam against, and its soundness text admits inherited-credit and __wrapped__ doors.

**Probes.** They are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1230efe6-3e44-5eb6-ad91-35910fea5db9/scratchpad/design/judge2/: probe_narrow.py, probe_narrow2.py, probe_flaky.py, probe_v5m.py, probe_lb.py, with fixtures jfx.py and jfx2.py.
